603400d77cfff554.title: India’s TB deaths fall 38% since 2015, outpacing global decline: WHO report
603400d77cfff554.summary: New Delhi: India has recorded a 38% reduction in tuberculosis (TB) mortality since 2015, outperforming the global decline of 35%, the Union health ministry said on Thursday. Highlighted in the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 released on Thursday, the findings also showed that the country achieved a 94% treatment success rate among drug-susceptible TB patients. According to the WHO report, India’s estimated TB mortality rate dropped from 280 per million people in 2015 to 180 per million in 2025. Meanwhile, a nationally representative TB prevalence survey conducted in 2025 by the Indian Council of Medical Research—National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis (ICMR-NIRT) has been shared with the WHO. The findings are currently under technical review, after which the WHO will publish an updated country profile for India. The health ministry added that 96% of India’s TB programme funding requirements are now met through domestic resources. The ministry also highlighted how the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan has transformed detection through technological innovation. Between December 2024 and November 2026, more than 250 million people were brought under TB screening. Authorities conducted over 11 crore chest X-rays—using portable, AI-enabled diagnostic tools—alongside more than 30 million rapid molecular nucleic acid amplification tests (NAAT). This identified 4.86 million new TB cases, including 1.49 million asymptomatic patients. The first intensified 100-day campaign under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan was launched on 7 December 2024, across 347 high-priority districts in 33 states and Union territories before being expanded nationwide. A second intensified 100-day campaign was launched on 24 March 2026, focusing on screening in 158,000 high-risk villages and wards, congregate settings, and vulnerable populations. 9600c1ce84962ac5.title: Trump endorses former Apple CEO Tim Cook to replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO: ‘A legend replaces a legend’
9600c1ce84962ac5.summary: Hours after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang tendered his resignation from the chief executive officer (CEO) position amid the spy affair scandal, US President Donald Trump said, "A legend should replace a legend," and endorsed former Apple Inc. chief executive Tim Cook's name. "NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend! (sic)," Trump said. While President Trump's public endorsement of Tim Cook drew widespread attention, neither Nvidia nor Apple has issued an official statement regarding Cook's potential cross-company migration Cook stepped down after a 15-year stint as Apple's CEO in September and is now executive chairman at the iPhone-maker. The tech giant has appointed the company's Chief Financial Officer, Colette Kress, as the interim CEO and said the "board has initiated a search for a permanent CEO." Nvidia has also restructured its governance, appointing Harvey C Jones as the company's first-ever Chair of the Board. Seeking to reassure investors ahead of its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results, scheduled for November 17, Jones said, “The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.” Interim CEO Colette Kress also expressed confidence in the company's direction, stating, "We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead." Huang, who co-founded the tech giant, has been embroiled in the controversy ever since reports claimed he had an extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. 6f68af2d20b39185.title: CPI(M) leader P. Rajeeve flays police action against protesters in Keralam’s Thiruvananthapuram
6f68af2d20b39185.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 12:30 am IST - KOCHI Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] central committee member P. Rajeeve has termed Wednesday night’s police action against protesters in Thiruvananthapuram and the removal to hospital of Valarmathi S., secretary of the action council and convener of the lower primary school teacher (LPST) rank holders’ protest committee, who was on a hunger strike, as anti-democratic. The government must specify which court order within six months of the United Democratic Front (UDF) assuming power that it relied on for such actions. Moreover, it owes an explanation on why it “went back” on an earlier assurance to extend the time frame for Public Service Commission rank lists. Agitations are being “suppressed”, while social media accounts are being closed down, he told the media here on Thursday. Likewise, the government that is finding fault with the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB) is taking credit for projects that were taken up under it. In another move, the government is preparing to inaugurate the construction work of the KIIFB-funded digital park, whose foundation stone was laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi when the Left Democratic Front was in power in the State, Mr. Rajeeve said. The project was completed at a cost of ₹115.29 crore, according to the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO). a6a8b1604feeb9bd.title: How to invest abroad through GIFT City: A step-by-step guide
a6a8b1604feeb9bd.summary: Resident Indians looking to invest abroad can do so through dollar-denominated funds based in GIFT City, the international financial centre in Gujarat. This offers an alternative to investing directly in foreign stocks through overseas brokers, a route examined in an earlier Business Standard article . Here is how to invest through GIFT City, from choosing a fund to transferring money. The route has drawn interest because many international mutual funds from domestic fund houses have stopped taking fresh money. The mutual fund industry as a whole has reached the $7 billion overseas investment limit set by the regulators, and funds based in GIFT City are not subject to that limit. One attraction is regulatory oversight. GIFT City funds come under the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), an Indian regulator. Investors using overseas brokers may have limited recourse through Indian regulators if something goes wrong, says Deepesh Raghaw, a Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi)-registered investment advisor and founder of PersonalFinancePlan.in. Those seeking to avoid cross-border disputes may prefer Indian funds or the GIFT City route, he says. Another reason is to hold assets in dollars. The rupee has tended to weaken against the dollar over time, so dollar assets can cushion that fall. Hema Thakkar, head of business development (alternatives) at PPFAS, says investors use these funds to build a dollar corpus for goals like a child’s education abroad, where the bills will be in dollars. A Balasubramanian, managing director and chief executive of Aditya Birla Sun Life Asset Management Company (AMC), also cites overseas education and travel. The market, however, is still developing. GIFT City was established primarily to attract foreign and non-resident Indian (NRI) investment into India, Raghaw says, and outbound retail funds remain a small segment. 6a94123090634351.title: As Chennai Corporation intensifies planting of saplings, waterlogging emerges a deterrent to green cover expansion
6a94123090634351.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 12:52 am IST - CHENNAI Chennai Corporation has started planting two lakh saplings this Northeast monsoon as it seeks to increase green cover in the city from 18% to 33% in a few years. However, waterlogging in several vacant lands, coupled with predominantly clayey soil conditions, remains a challenge to increasing the green cover. Chennai Corporation Commissioner G.S.Sameeran said: “Based on the intensity of rainfall, planting of an estimated 1.5-2 lakh saplings can be achieved by December 2026, in addition to planting 1.36 lakh saplings from June 2026. Our overall target is 12 lakh for this year. It is proposed to prioritise the planting of native tree species such as Mahilam, Poovarasu, Pungam, Punnai, Neer Marudhu, Neem, Jamun and other tropical avenue trees like Peltophorum, Tabebuia, Spathodea and Cassia that are ecologically suitable and well-adapted to the local soil and climatic conditions.” Pointing to site constraints, Dr. Sameeran said waterlogging in several vacant lands, coupled with predominantly clayey soil conditions, posed challenges to tree planting activities and affected the suitability of certain sites for tree planting. As per the Chennai City Biodiversity Index (2025) and the recent assessment by Anna University (2026), Chennai’s existing green cover is estimated to be in the range of 15–18%. Chennai Corporation officials said the civic body proposed to progressively increase Chennai’s green cover towards the 33% benchmark through a comprehensive and integrated approach, comprising large-scale tree plantation across suitable locations, development of urban forests, avenue and roadside plantations, restoration of degraded parks and green spaces. GCC intends to promote partnerships with educational institutions, industries and other organisations. c48eaaec43dc5cd8.title: No government school will be closed due to low enrolment: Minister Rajmohan
c48eaaec43dc5cd8.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:13 am IST - VELLORE Minister for School Education, Tamil Development, Information and Publicity, Rajmohan, addresses the Achievers Appreciation Day at VIT Vellore on Thursday. G.Viswanathan, founder & chancellor, VIT, is also seen. | Photo Credit: C. VENKATACHALAPATHY Minister for School Education Rajmohan on Thursday said that the State government will not shut down even a single government school on the basis of low enrollment of students. In his inaugural address at the felicitation ceremony, organised by VIT Vellore, for headmasters of government and government-aided schools in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur and Tiruvannamalai districts that secured 100 per cent pass results in Board examinations for 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26, Mr. Rajmohan said that since the new government formed six months ago, no government school has been closed, citing low enrollment. “New teaching methods such as teaching mathematics through stories and improvements in curriculum have been introduced to boost enrolment in government schools,” he said. G. Viswanathan, founder and chancellor, VIT, highlighted the need to set up a committee to study the impact of the Right to Education Act’s policy of ensuring pass results on overall educational quality and to examine whether the policy need to be reviewed. It comes in the backdrop of closure of around 94,000 government schools as against 51,000 private schools that were opened in the country in the past decade. “In Tamil Nadu, 246 government schools had been shut during the same period. At present, around 1,200 schools have zero enrolment,” he said. Sankar Viswanathan and Sekar Viswanathan, vice presidents, VIT, and Premalatha, District Educational Officer (Vellore), were among others present on the occasion. 4df5d58432614d75.title: Dhinakaran urges quality checks on Children’s Day cakes
4df5d58432614d75.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:11 am IST - CHENNAI Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran. | Photo Credit: ASHOK R AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran on Thursday urged the Tamil Nadu government to ensure that cakes procured for distribution to students of government and government-aided schools on Children’s Day were subjected to proper quality checks before being distributed. Mr. Dhinakaran alleged that cakes purchased from various companies had been lying unattended in vehicles for the past four days without proper storage or preservation, raising concerns over their safety. Pointing out that the cakes had reportedly been transported over long distances, Mr. Dhinakaran in a social media post said it was essential to verify their manufacturing and expiry dates, storage conditions and quality. He said reports of improper storage had caused concern among parents, particularly in view of earlier complaints about the quality of food served under the school breakfast and mid-day meal schemes. Mr. Dhinakaran urged the School Education Department to ensure that only safe and quality cakes reached children. aba73b5290c1fc47.title: Five e-scooters catch fire in Ranipet
aba73b5290c1fc47.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:02 am IST - RANIPET Police said that an electrical short circuit could have been the reason for the incident. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Five electric scooters caught fire at the showroom at Kaveripakkam village near Walajah town in Ranipet on Thursday. Police said that Y. Suresh, 49, a resident of Walajah town, was running an e-scooter showroom on Bazaar Street in Kaveripakkam village near Walajah town. Initial inquiry revealed that, Suresh reportedly plugged in the vehicles to charge the batteries, but apparently forgot to disconnect the power supply before closing the showroom on Wednesday. On Thursday, a few residents alerted Suresh about smoke in the showroom. Police said that when he opened the showroom, Suresh saw that five e-scooters were gutted and 10 other vehicles were damaged in the fire. Based on the alert, firefighters doused the blaze in the outlet. Police said that an electrical short circuit could have been the reason for the incident. They also said that charging the vehicle for too long could have caused the fire, as damaged vehicles were plugged in for charging. A case was registered and further probe is underway. The police said this was not the first time that electric scooters had caught fire. In February 2023, an electric scooter parked on the veranda of a house in Vaniyambadi near Tirupattur caught fire. The vehicle was left to charge the previous night before the owner of the vehicle S. Ihsanuallh, went to sleep. The fire gutted his bike and the meter box. e6f9d26de74449d2.title: SIR: Draft electoral roll released in Vellore, nearby districts
e6f9d26de74449d2.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:01 am IST - VELLORE District Collector P.S.Leela Alex releasing the Special draft electoral rolls in the presence of all political parties in Vellore on Thursday. | Photo Credit: C. Venkatachalapathy The draft electoral rolls for Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 2027 were released on Thursday for Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur and Tiruvannamalai districts, with women voters higher than men voters. District Election Officer (DEO) P.S. c416df0d5ce20919.title: Residents urge GCC to stop dumping of waste in Perungudi dumpyard
c416df0d5ce20919.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 12:35 am IST - CHENNAI Citing rising public health issues, residents have demanded that the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) stop dumping waste in the Perungudi dumpyard. Residents’ associations have planned to launch protests against the dumping. MCN Nagar and State Bank Colony Welfare Association secretary, M. Krishnamurthy, said: “The dumpyard generates leachate when rainwater filters through waste. Leachate seeps into the groundwater and spreads to all the surrounding areas.” K. Kalaiselvam, secretary of the Federation of Thoraipakkam Residents’ Welfare Associations, said the site released toxic air pollutants. Residents have also demanded real-time monitoring of air pollution in the areas near the dumpyard. A. Francis, president of the Federation of Thoraipakkam Residents’ Welfare Associations, said: “Biomining work is progressing at a snail’s pace. It was expected to be completed by 2024, but only 100 acres have been reclaimed so far. Residents are facing the risk of health complications. Chennai Corporation should stop dumping waste and close the dumpyard in Perungudi.” Following protests by north Chennai residents a few years ago, residents of south Chennai are also expected to launch an agitation against the dumpyard. 9a2986172ae2e393.title: Veeramani chargesheet was based on plaint lodged by minor girl
9a2986172ae2e393.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 12:36 am IST - Chennai The chargesheet against Veeramani and two of his drivers, submitted in the designated court for POCSO Act cases, was based on a complaint lodged by a minor girl. According to police sources, the survivor alleged in her complaint that she was sexually exploited by Veeramani. She had identified the octogenarian businessman during an identification process conducted by the special investigation team (SIT). Veeramani is facing seven cases under the POCSO Act and a case of abetment to suicide of a minor in 2004. The cases involve more than 10 survivors who alleged that they were sexually abused by him. The SIT was in the process of finalising the investigation in a few more cases. Prakash Kanniah, one of the accused wanted in connection with the cases, is believed to be in the U.K. After the police took steps to revoke his passport and obtain an arrest warrant from the designated court, which is required to issue a Red Corner notice, he was likely to return sometime this week, a source said. Veeramani and his drivers Parthiban and Babu were charged under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code, POCSO Act and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. 0a281acd971cdf13.title: Manappuram Finance Q2 results: Profit jumps over 3-fold to ₹701 crore
0a281acd971cdf13.summary: Gold loan financier Manappuram Finance Ltd on Thursday reported a more than three-fold year-on-year increase in its consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 701 crore for the September quarter of FY27. The company had posted a PAT of Rs 217.31 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal. On a sequential basis, net profit rose 20 per cent from Rs 585 crore in the June quarter. Total income increased to Rs 3,312 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 2,275 crore in the year-ago period, the company said in a regulatory filing. The company's total assets under management (AUM) stood at Rs 73,303 crore as of September 2026, registering a year-on-year growth of 60 per cent. Gold Loan AUM surged 92.5 per cent YoY to Rs 60,640 crore at the end of the September quarter. Shares of Manappuram Finance settled 0.23 per cent lower at Rs 320.25 apiece on the BSE.

4c1e828f57f7883e.title: Gang held for possession of 500 kg red sanders near Sholinghur in Ranipet
4c1e828f57f7883e.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:12 am IST - RANIPET Officials said that the accused told them the consignment was meant to deliver to agents in Chennai. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT A gang of three persons was arrested after the Forest Department officials seized seven red sander logs weighing around 500 kg from a car near Sholinghur town in Ranipet district on Thursday. The accused were identified them as S. Ramakrishnan, 39, V. Devinthran, 41, and T. Bhagyaraj, 35, all residents of Ranipet. Officials said that they spotted a speeding car during a patrol led by forest range officer N. Saravanan in the Neelakandaranpet Reserve Forest (RF). The team tried to stop the car along with the help of police personnel, but in vain. Forest officials and the police chased the car for around 500 metres and cornered the car at an isolated location near Sholinghur town. The team arrested the three persons after they found red sanders in the vehicle. Officials said that the accused told them the consignment was meant to deliver to agents in Chennai. The gang learnt the forests around Sholinghur town have a sizable number of red sanders that are cultivated by the Forest Department as part of an afforestation programme over a decade ago. A case was registered and the gang members were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. The seized wooden logs were sent to the government incense sticks making unit in Tirupattur. c3ecb8e0c4add364.title: Saqib takes 7 wickets on debut before rain disrupts Pakistan-Sri Lanka first cricket Test
c3ecb8e0c4add364.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 02:44 am IST - RAWALPINDI Pakistan's Saqib Khan bowls during the fourth day of the first Test cricket match between Pakistan and Sri Lanka, in Rawalpindi, Pakistan, on November 12, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP New fast bowler Saqib Khan's seven-wicket haul led Pakistan's comeback against Sri Lanka on a rain-affected day four of the first cricket test on Thursday. Saqib's dream figures of 7-130 on debut helped Sri Lanka collapse to 446 all out after resuming on a formidable 404-4. Sri Lanka eked out a first-innings lead of 12 runs. Pakistan reached 57-1 in 21.2 overs of its second innings midway into the second session when stumps was called at 3:05 p.m. for bad light followed by rain. Pakistan leads by 45 runs at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. At the crease were Azan Awais, on 22 after he was dropped on 17 by captain Kusal Mendis behind the wickets, and Mohammad Taha, one of Pakistan's four debutants who has followed his first innings half-century with 24 not out off 55 balls. The 31-year-old Saqib made full use of perfect bowling conditions on the fourth morning with incisive swing to rattle Sri Lanka. The visitor lost its last six wickets for 42 runs in a seven-wicket first session after only one wicket fell on day two. Saqib became only the fourth man after Mohammad Nazir, Mohammad Zahid and Abrar Ahmed to grab seven wickets in an innings on test debut for Pakistan. “My strength is to bowl out-swingers and I did exactly that today under favorable overcast conditions,” Saqib said. “Yesterday was a bad day for us because we couldn't bowl the way we would have liked to, but coach Mike Hesson told us in the dressing room that if we hit the off stump line and bowl out-swingers we will get wickets.” Saqib kisses the pitchThe greenish pitch on which Sri Lanka lost only Kamindu Mendis on Wednesday sprung to life in on Thursday in overcast conditions. In a relentless eight-over spell, Saqib grabbed 5-25 as centurions Dhananjaya de Silva and captain

Sessions Judge Ash K. Bal sentenced the 37-year-old accused in the incident which took place in October 2021. The relative was convicted for trespassing into the minor’s house and raping her. Special Public Prosecutor Pious Mathew and Francis Pious and Ancy Philip appeared for the prosecution. 2d5df521f158a3de.title: 'Reunification is certain': Xi vows to bring Taiwan under China's control
2d5df521f158a3de.summary: President Xi Jinping on Thursday vowed to bring Taiwan under Chinese control, saying the "complete reunification" of the motherland is an "unwavering historical mission" for the ruling Communist Party of China (CPC) and will certainly be achieved. Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a ceremony marking the 160th birth anniversary of Sun Yat-sen, one of China's nationalist leaders who is revered on both sides of the Taiwan Strait. He pledged to accommodate the island's realities but took a hard line against separatism. "Resolving the Taiwan question and realising the complete reunification of the motherland is an unwavering historical mission for the CPC, the shared aspiration of all Chinese people, and a natural requirement for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation," Xi was quoted as saying by the state-run Xinhua news agency. China views Taiwan as a rebel province that must be reunified

flags: Timeline Impossibility: Claiming a fully indigenous civil aircraft will be ready in two years is highly implausible given the typical 10-15 year development cycle for new commercial aircraft programs.
Policy Mismatch: The UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) scheme focuses on regional connectivity using existing aircraft, not the development of a new indigenous civil aircraft platform.

Official Denial: Indian government officials and aviation experts have repeatedly stated that India does not have the current industrial capacity or active program to build a new civil aircraft in such a short timeframe.

Source Reliability: While Business Standard is a reputable source, the specific claim contradicts widely reported facts about India's aviation industry status and ongoing projects like the Tejas fighter jet (military, not civil) or the lack of a dedicated civil aircraft manufacturer.

ed21403ea2855a3e.title: Punjab man wins ₹1.5 crore lottery a day after daughter Barkat's birth: ‘We wanted a boy’
ed21403ea2855a3e.summary: A baby girl born into a financially struggling family in Punjab turned out to be a source of unexpected fortune for her parents. Just a day after 24-year-old carpenter Yudhvir Singh welcomed his daughter, he won ₹ 1.5 crore in a state lottery. The win came after some relatives had told him, ‘We wanted a boy’. Singh now credits his daughter for changing the family's fortunes and has named her Barkat, meaning prosperity. According to a report by The Tribune, Singh, a resident of Bareta town in Punjab's Mansa district, bagged the first prize in the Punjab State Dear 200 Monthly Lottery. His daughter was born on November 6, while the lottery results were declared on November 7. The proud father chose the name Barkat, which means prosperity, for his daughter following the unexpected windfall. Singh had bought the winning ticket on November 4 from a lottery stall in Budhlada. He was accompanying his pregnant wife, Harman, to a hospital in Mansa for a medical check-up when he made the purchase. The carpenter had not intended to buy a lottery ticket that day. He had stopped at the stall while getting his mobile phone number ported and decided to try his luck. However, the decision did not go down well with his wife initially, particularly given the family's financial difficulties. The couple was already repaying a loan taken to build their two-room house and had additional medical expenses to manage ahead of their first child's arrival. Singh recalled that Harman had questioned why he was spending money on a lottery ticket when they needed funds for hospital bills. He also said that the private hospital had declined to offer even a ₹ 5,000 reduction in their bill. For the family, which was struggling to meet its expenses, the lottery ticket had been an unplanned purchase. Little did Singh know that it would eventually bring him a prize worth ₹ 1.5 crore. ce56b9828f6343d4.title: Farm-fire incidents fall 11.5% across six northern states to 9,590
ce56b9828f6343d4.summary: This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. Farm-fire incidents across six northern Indian states fell by 11.5% to 9,590 since the start of the stubble-burning season on 15 September, from 10,832 in the year-ago period, showed satellite-based data from the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR). Punjab continued to account for the largest share of farm fires from 15 September to 10 November, reporting 5,002 incidents, followed by Madhya Pradesh with 2,145 and Rajasthan with 1,335. Uttar Pradesh recorded 689 cases, while Uttarakhand and Haryana reported 213 and 206 incidents, respectively. During the year-ago period, Punjab recorded 4,195 farm-fire incidents, followed by Madhya Pradesh (2,517) and Uttar Pradesh (1,902). Rajasthan reported 1,385 incidents, while Uttarakhand and Haryana recorded 470 and 363, respectively. Farm-fire incidents across the six states have consistently declined, from 46,399 during 15 September-10 November 2022 to 36,415 in 2023, 17,314 in 2024, 10,832 in 2025, and 9,590 in 2026. The decline in farm fires is significant, given their contribution to Delhi’s pollution. While they account for around 2.25% of the city’s annual pollution, their share rises to 12-40% during the winter stubble-burning season. The National Capital Region (NCR) grapples with poor air quality throughout the year, with conditions typically worsening between November and February as slower winds trap pollutants over the region for longer. According to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data, Delhi recorded its worst daily average Air Quality Index (AQI) of 2026 on 6 November, at 382. The average AQI stood at 376 on Diwali, 8 November, making it the most polluted Diwali in five years. Delhi’s air quality has remained in the poor to very poor categories so far this month. 173ade0ce7a623c0.title: Great Trigonometrical Survey stations in Tamil Nadu documented, published in five volumes
173ade0ce7a623c0.summary: Published - November 12, 2026 02:12 am IST - CHENNAI The Department of Survey and Settlement and the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology have documented the Great Trigonometrical Survey (GTS) stations in the State and published the documentation in five volumes. According to an official release, during British rule, the Great Trigonometrical Survey was launched by Colonel William Lambton at St. Thomas Mount in Chennai on April 10, 1802. The survey continued for 70 years until 1871 using theodolite instruments. As part of the exercise, Great Trigonometrical Survey stations were established across India, including at several locations in Tamil Nadu. These stations are under the jurisdiction of the Survey of India. The Tamil Nadu government granted permission for a comprehensive exercise to identify all the GTS stations in the State, conduct surveys, map and document them, and take steps to preserve them. The initiative also aims to facilitate future modern surveying activities in the State by using the geo-coordinates of these stations. Accordingly, officials from the Department of Survey and Settlement and TNSDA jointly conducted an extensive field survey, identified all the GTS stations in Tamil Nadu and documented their details. Based on their documentation, they have published five volumes titled ‘Documentation of the Great Trigonometrical Survey Stations in Tamil Nadu’. With the objective of ensuring the preservation of the GTS stations in the districts, the Director of Survey and Settlement has distributed the volumes to District Collectors and district-level officials of the Survey Department, the release added. 55328a107c9ab561.title: Govt approves high-capacity power corridor to support clean energy boom
55328a107c9ab561.summary: Existing 765-kV lines would require more transmission corridors and land ​requirements to carry electricity India has approved plans for a high-capacity power transmission ​corridor to carry clean electricity from its ​western generation hubs to growing industrial and urban ‌demand centres in the east. The project is estimated to cost nearly ₹68,800 crore ($7.34 billion) and take about six years to complete. The 1,150-kilovolt (kV) system would be India's highest-voltage power network, allowing the dispatch of much larger volumes of electricity nationwide than present 765-kV lines. India's national transmission panel approved the project, according to minutes of a ‌meeting released late Tuesday. India is adding renewable energy at a record pace along with battery storage, as it targets 500 gigawatts of non-fossil power generation by 2030, from more than 300 GW now. Existing 765-kV lines would require more transmission corridors and land ​requirements to carry electricity. A 1,150-kV network can carry substantially more power, ‌moving the same amount of electricity along fewer lines and less land, with smaller transmission losses. ​The ‌network is being planned as renewable energy capacity expands rapidly ‌in western states such as Rajasthan, while electricity demand rises in eastern industrial hubs such as Odisha. The ​first phase will ​link the states of Chhattisgarh, Odisha and West Bengal and connect with a 6,000-megawatt high-voltage transmission ‌system carrying renewable ​power from Rajasthan's Bhadla solar region. 70873b32005f1a70.title: Moody's raises India's FY27 growth forecast to 7% on broad-based momentum
70873b32005f1a70.summary: Moody's Ratings on Wednesday said the Indian economy is expected to grow at a higher rate of 7 per cent in the current fiscal, led by broad-based economic momentum and energy supply shock resilience. In its Global Macro Outlook 2027-28, Moody's, however, said that near-term risks to growth persist as household consumption remains vulnerable to "intensifying and broadening price pressures", with headline inflation close to the upper end of the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) 2-6 per cent target range, while a deficient southwest monsoon and strengthening El Nino conditions will weigh on agricultural output and rural demand. "India's broad-based economic momentum and demonstrated resilience to the energy supply shock warrant upward revisions to our 2026-27 growth forecasts to 7 per cent from 6.5 per cent," it said. a5ba4c5b09b8a120.title: Keralam government centralising power in Chief Minister’s office: Pinarayi Vijayan
a5ba4c5b09b8a120.summary: Published - November 12, 2026 02:17 am IST - KASARAGOD Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan has accused the Keralam government of concentrating decision-making powers in the hands of the Chief Minister, alleging that even ministers are being kept in the dark about important decisions. He said the situation was unprecedented in the State and called for a judicial investigation into what he described as suspicious administrative actions. Speaking at the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] political explanation meeting at Chathurakkinar in Madikkai, Mr. Vijayan questioned how a Minister, who is also the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee president, could remain unaware of major decisions concerning his own department. He said governance was being conducted without proper coordination between departments, with the Chief Minister taking decisions independently. Referring to the electricity purchase agreement with GNA, Mr. Vijayan said the Minister concerned had earlier said that he was unaware of the decision to enter into the agreement. The Minister was reportedly unaware even when the decision to abandon the agreement was taken, he said. He also alleged that attempts were being made to create an artificial power shortage to benefit corporate monopolies. f718cf96c748fda0.title: India eyes wind turbine revamp to boost output, bypass land woes
f718cf96c748fda0.summary: India is weighing replacing aging wind turbines with larger, more efficient machines to boost generation at older farms without having to acquire more land. As much as 8 gigawatts of capacity using old and smaller turbines can be upgraded with modern units, according to a preliminary assessment by the Indian Wind Turbine Manufacturers Association, Chief Executive Officer Aditya Pyasi said in an interview. The lobby group is in talks with federal and state governments to finalize a plan that could help increase capacity at those sites by almost 50%. Wind power has become increasingly important for India to meet peak electricity demand after sunset. Although the country’s green power capacity has quadrupled since 2014, wind installations have lagged far behind solar, with land acquisition and securing right-of-way remaining major hurdles to faster deployment. That — coupled with limited battery storage — has left the grid struggling to absorb excess daytime generation, forcing solar curtailments while creating shortfalls at night. Installations reached a record 6.3 gigawatts in 2025. Still, wind project deployment remains below the pace needed to meet India’s 2030 goal of 500 gigawatts clean power capacity. Replacing older turbines of as much as 2 megawatts with modern 3- to 5-megawatt units at existing sites could help sidestep land-access hurdles. 63eac8bb310fb096.title: Kerala High Court orders government to ready adequate medicines, vehicles at mental health centres by November 24
63eac8bb310fb096.summary: Published - November 12, 2026 02:16 am IST - KOCHI Government Mental Health Centre, Thrissur. | Photo Credit: FILE PHOTO Stating that assurances alone are not sufficient, and they have to translate into action, the Kerala High Court has directed the government to make available adequate medicines and vehicles in mental health centres by November 24. A Division Bench of Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji, who had earlier this year visited the centres in Thiruvananthapuram, Thrissur, and Kozhikode acceded to the Advocate General’s request to file an action taken report by the same day on the construction of compound walls and the appointment of necessary personnel at the centres. This was after the Advocate General submitted that the construction of compound walls around the centres was progressing at a good speed. On the appointment of personnel, he sought another two weeks’ time, saying that there had been a change of incumbent in the post of Secretary, Health and Family Welfare department, and that he was in the process of evaluating the files concerned. The matter has been listed for hearing on November 24. The High Court had in September expressed satisfaction at the government’s decision to rename mental health centres as “happiness and wellness centres”, observing that the (hitherto) stigmatisation of patients, their caregivers, and the centres as a whole was something one could not be oblivious to. The Advocate General had informed the court then that the government was looking into infrastructure and staff vacancy issues at the centres with ‘full sincerity’. flags: Exaggerated scale: '40 containers' is a trivially small volume for a major FTA dispute involving global giants like Pernod Ricard and Diageo; such a minor logistical hiccup would not be characterized as the 'first major hurdle' or 'first major dispute' in a headline.

Unsubstantiated specific claim: The specific detail of a '150% tariff' being sought versus a '75% duty' assurance is highly specific and lacks corroboration from major international news sources or official trade announcements as of the current date.

Mischaracterization of FTA status: The India-UK FTA is still under negotiation and has not yet been ratified or implemented. Therefore, it cannot face a 'dispute' under the treaty's dispute settlement mechanism, nor can it have 'assurances' of reduced duties that are being violated in a legal sense. Customs disputes during the negotiation phase are common but not 'FTA disputes'.

Source reliability: Livemint is a reputable Indian financial news source, but the specific framing of a minor port hold-up as a 'major FTA dispute' suggests potential sensationalism or confusion between a routine customs query and a treaty-level conflict.

c6eae5ba3ca34ffc.title: Offering food, best dharma
c6eae5ba3ca34ffc.summary: Published - November 12, 2026 05:22 am IST Offering food to others is the best dharma, said R. Narayanan in a discourse. There is nothing to equal this, says Tiruvalluvar. In his Tirumanthiram, Tirumoolar says we should offer a vilva leaf to Lord Siva, grass to a cow, and food to fellow human beings. More importantly, we must always use sweet words. Tiruvalluvar says that even nectar, which confers immortality, must be shared with others. Ilayankudi Maranar was one of the 63 Nayanmars praised by Sekkizhar in his Periya Puranam. Maranar was wealthy. He honoured devotees of Siva by washing their feet with scented water. He then offered them a lavish meal, which did not lack any flavour. The Lord wanted to show the world how generous Ilayankudi Maranar could be even in poverty. He made sure that Maranar lost his wealth. Eventually, he was left with nothing but a tiled house and a small plot of land. One night, after Maranar had sown seeds in his field, it rained heavily. That night, Siva, in the guise of a Saivite devotee, arrived at Maranar’s doorstep. Maranar’s wife asked her husband to fetch the grains that had been sown that morning. She cleaned the grains, and used it to cook rice for the visitor. Usually, the grains used for sowing were never used for cooking, because they ensured that a farmer would be able to grow his next crop. So, something that would take care of a farmer’s future would never be used for food. But Maranar and his wife broke that rule, when they cooked for the mendicant. Greens grown in the backyard were also used to prepare tasty dishes. Since there was no firewood, Maranar’s wife used a wooden beam from their house as firewood. When the couple was about to serve food, the sleeping guest woke and revealed Himself as Lord Siva. He blessed them and said they would reach Sivaloka. 74b09dff258a7741.title: Cochin shipyard, SFO Technologies jointly develop sophisticated laser arc welding technology
74b09dff258a7741.summary: Published - November 12, 2026 02:03 am IST - KOCHI Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) and the Kochi-based SFO Technologies Private Limited have unveiled what is claimed to be the country’s first indigenously designed and manufactured hybrid laser arc welding (HLAW) technology. The announcement was made at the inauguration of the Advanced Laser Engineering Centre and HLAW R&D facility at NeST Hitek Park, Kalamassery. The facility was inaugurated by Jose V.J., chairman and managing director, CSL, and N. Jehangir, chairman and managing director, SFO Technologies. Jointly developed by CSL and SFO Technologies, the HLAW system integrates laser welding, conventional arc welding, robotics, and advanced automation, powered by a high-power fibre laser source indigenously developed by SFO Technologies, claimed a communication. The technology is expected to deliver faster welding speeds, deeper penetration, lower distortion, and improved weld consistency across shipbuilding, defence, heavy engineering, railways, energy, and other strategic manufacturing sectors like large tanks and wagons for improving productivity, claimed the developers in a statement. Jointly developed by CSL and SFO Technologies, the HLAW system integrates laser welding, conventional arc welding, robotics, and advanced automation, powered by a high-power fibre laser source indigenously developed by SFO Technologies, claimed a communication. The technology is expected to deliver faster welding speeds, deeper penetration, lower distortion, and improved weld consistency across shipbuilding, defence, heavy engineering, railways, energy, and other strategic manufacturing sectors like large tanks and wagons for improving productivity, claimed the developers in a statement. be3ca298a0b0f246.title: Govt raises price cap for officers' electronic devices to ₹1.8 lakh
be3ca298a0b0f246.summary: The central government has raised the price ceiling of laptops, tablets, or similar devices for its eligible officers to Rs 1.8 lakh plus taxes, and officials can retain them for personal use after four years. The Finance Ministry's Expenditure Department on November 10 issued revised guidelines on the purchase of Note Book /Laptop by ministries/departments of the central government. Central government employees of Sections Officer rank and above will be eligible for the devices. "...it has been decided that laptop; tablet; notepad; ultra-book; notebook; devices of similar categories may be issued to eligible officers for discharge of official work," it said. The new guidelines replace the July 2023 instructions on similar purchases of gadgets. The 2023 guidelines explicitly mentioned the purchase of mobile devices, which is not mentioned in the November 10, 2026, office memorandum. As per the new guidelines, the cost of the device shall not be more than Rs 1.50 lakh + taxes. Howe

ab321892aff36ee2.summary: Published - November 12, 2026 03:14 am IST Mr. Duncan J. McDougald, a Canadian Industrial magnate, Director of the Canadian National Railways, the Canadian Government Merchant Marine and director of several other important Canadian enterprises and a prominent financier of Toronto, arrived in Madras this morning. Mr. McDougald is now on a pleasure trip round the world. He left Canada in September and has already toured in Japan, China and the Malay States. While in India, he will take the opportunity of studying the conditions of Indian railways. In the course of a talk with a representative of the Associated Press on his arrival this morning Mr. McDougald said that he was very much impressed with the generous hospitality and courtesy he received from the officials of the Indian railways. The Canadian National Railways of which he was a director ran length of twenty-four thousand miles in Canada and the United States of America. Mr. McDougald informed the interviewer that possibly the most spectacular innovation on the Canadian National Railways was the installation of a radio service over all high class express trains of the Canadian National Railway. af1c35f25bd603ad.title: MP alleges intelligence failure over Nanjangud drug racket
af1c35f25bd603ad.summary: Updated - November 12, 2026 12:49 am IST - MYSURU Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Mysuru MP Mysuru-Kodagu MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar has accused the Congress government of a serious intelligence failure following the alleged busting of an inter-State drug racket operating under the guise of a banana plantation in Nanjangud by the Keralam Police. In a statement here, Mr. Yaduveer said it was shocking that the racket operating on Karnataka soil was detected by the police of a neighbouring State rather than the Karnataka Police or the State intelligence wing. He said this was not an isolated incident, pointing out that Maharashtra Police and central investigating agencies had intervened in recent years to expose organised drug networks operating in Mysuru. “Such incidents raised serious questions about the effectiveness of the State’s intelligence machinery,” he added. Questioning the government’s repeated claims of intensifying its crackdown on narcotics and strengthening police surveillance, he asked how an illegal operation allegedly conducted under the cover of agricultural activity could go unnoticed by the local police. He alleged that the repeated involvement of police forces from other States and central agencies in detecting alleged criminal networks operating in Karnataka reflected serious lapses in law enforcement and intelligence gathering. The Congress government should take moral responsibility for the failure, he demanded. Mr. Yaduveer also sought to know why the State intelligence wing had failed to detect the racket, what surveillance mechanisms were in place to identify organised drug networks and who would be held accountable for the alleged lapses. Calling for a comprehensive investigation, he urged the government to uncover the entire network behind the racket, fix accountability for the alleged intelligence lapses, strengthen inter-State police coordination and take stringent action against all those involved. Published -

a45eb564a9e1ba47.title: Hijack threat note found on Air India flight, plane taken to isolation bay
a45eb564a9e1ba47.summary: A hijack threat note found in the washroom of a Mumbai-bound Air India flight before take-off on Wednesday morning prompted security officials to park the aircraft in an isolation bay of the airport here, an official said. The flight was scheduled to depart at 10.20 am. The note threatening that the plane would be hijacked at 11.10 am was found in the washroom just before the departure of the flight, Kolkata airport director Vikram Singh said. All the passengers who had boarded the aircraft were deboarded, and it was taken to the isolation bay, he said. Security protocols were immediately activated, and the aircraft was moved to an isolation bay for a thorough inspection and necessary precautionary measures, he said.

More than 19.13 lakh pilgrims visited Kedarnath, and over 8.84 lakh visited Yamunotri during this year's pilgrimage season. d8e130716c776d1d.summary: Moody's Ratings on Tuesday said it expects global credit conditions to weaken in 2027 due to higher financing costs and elevated energy prices. The Moody's Ratings' 2027 Global Credit Conditions Outlook report examines the key forces that could shape credit markets in the year ahead. It said AI investment will remain massive, but investors will increasingly focus on whether revenues and productivity gains justify the scale of spending. "Business model disruption will become more visible: some companies will gain from stronger demand and productivity, while others face more competition and weaker pricing power," Moody's Ratings said. Besides, Moody's expects government intervention through tariffs, regulation, export controls and strategic investment to play a growing role in credit outcomes. "As many of these tools can be introduced or reversed by executive action, policy can shift quickly, therefore this will continue to influence trade, capital allocation and competition in 2027

f7814ef3cf97c8de.title: FPIs turn net buyers in November, pump ₹53,739 crore into Indian equities
f7814ef3cf97c8de.summary: Foreign investors turned net buyers of Indian equities in November, infusing Rs 53,739 crore in the first nine days after two consecutive months of outflows, driven by the AI-led sell-off in global markets, strong domestic earnings growth and attractive large-cap valuations. The latest investment follows net outflows of Rs 34,843 crore in October and Rs 35,861 crore in September, according to data available with the depositories. "The sudden change in FPI stance was triggered by the AI sell-off in the US and other AI markets like South Korea, Taiwan and Japan. "This sell-off, in turn, was triggered by fears surrounding data centre spending in the US. The Democrats, who won both chambers of Congress, are opposed to indiscriminate data centre spending. They will demand guardrails for AI," said V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments. The AI-led sell-off has made India, widely regarded as a non-AI trade, an attractive destination for Foreign Portfolio Invest

Mahindra acknowledged that India does not make the most advanced chips or lead the race i

774c708eded497ec.summary: Transactions through the popular Unified Payments Interface (UPI) witnessed a 32 per cent surge in volume terms on Diwali driven by last-minute festival buying. UPI volume increased to 916.9 million on November 8 from 695.7 million transactions on the same day last year, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). In value terms, UPI transactions rose to Rs 90,029.43 crore on November 8 against Rs 88,350.79 crore last year. A day prior to Diwali, the transaction volume was 975.8 million resulting in transfer of Rs 1,36,118 crore. UPI is an instant payment system developed by the NPCI. NPCI, an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Indian Banks' Association (IBA), is an umbrella organisation for operating retail payments and settlement systems in India. 313f9bcf219cb166.title: No proposal to allot Central Secretariat club premises to anyone: Centre tells Delhi High Court
313f9bcf219cb166.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 04:50 am IST The Centre has informed the Delhi High Court that there is no proposal to allot the Central Secretariat Club premises to anyone at this stage. The submission was made while the court was hearing an interim application filed by the club seeking a stay on the Centre’s decision to withdraw its recognition and the subsequent eviction order. Taking note of the government’s submission, Justice Amit Mahajan said no interim directions were necessary at this stage. The court, however, permitted the club to remove its belongings from the premises within a week. “Considering the above, no order is required to be passed. The petitioners are permitted to take away their belongings in next one week. List on the date already fixed, that is, December 21, 2026,” the court said. The club, earlier known as Talkatora Club, has challenged the government’s decision to withdraw its recognition as well as an eviction order issued by the estate officer directing it to immediately vacate its premises in the President’s Estate. The interim relief was sought against the July 14, 2026 de-recognition order and the July 17, 2026 eviction order. During the November 5 hearing, the Centre’s counsel informed the court that there was no proposal to allot the premises to any party at present. According to the club, the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) arbitrarily, illegally and unconstitutionally withdrew its recognition on July 14. The petitioner said that instead of taking corrective action on its complaints regarding irregularities during the term of the ad hoc committee managing its affairs, the authorities first withdrew the recognition in February without issuing any show cause notice. It further contended, “the respondents are attempting to weaponise their own administrative failures and the misdeeds of their ad hoc committee to forcefully dispossess and extinguish a historic institution, in flagrant violation of Article 14 of the Constitutio

04b9e8c6ff989ba3.title: Karnataka-registered doctors may be allowed to practise in Kasaragod: Keralam Health Minister
04b9e8c6ff989ba3.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 02:04 am IST - KASARAGOD Keralam Health Minister K. Muraleedharan The Keralam government has recommended to the State Medical Council that doctors registered with the Karnataka Medical Council be allowed to practise in Kasaragod, considering the district’s special circumstances, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan has said. The medical council is expected to take a favourable decision on the recommendation soon, the Minister said while inaugurating ‘Kayakalpam’, a public outreach programme of the Health Minister. Government hospitals should have adequate number of doctors, nurses, pharmacists, and laboratory technicians, the Minister said, adding that additional posts had been sought. Their early sanction would considerably ease staff shortage in the district. The extension of the tenure of National Health Mission employees in Kasaragod till March 31 was also an indication of the government’s commitment to the district, he said. The Minister said that he would direct the authorities to convene a meeting of the Endosulfan cell soon. Periye in Kasaragod was among the four locations proposed by the government to the Centre for setting up an All India Institute of Medical Sciences, he said. Instructions had been issued to make hostel facilities available at the Kasaragod Medical College within two months. The construction of a hostel for nursing students would begin within three months, he added. The government would ensure the services of a forensic surgeon at the Kanhangad district hospital. A new building for the District Medical Office would be constructed at a cost of ₹4.8 crore. A BPCL outlet began operating beside the highway in September, less than 100 metres away. “The water in a nearby well first developed a chlorine-like smell in January. Later, there was a smell resembling soap and now petrol or diesel,” he said. According to Mr. Premraj, samples collected from six wells near three petrol pumps tested positive for petroleum hydrocarbon. The Health department subsequently issued notices warning residents against using the water for drinking, bathing, or other domestic purposes. c65d287d2023421b.summary: This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. New Delhi: After India's gram (chana) imports fell in FY26 from a record high a year earlier, the government is stepping up efforts to strengthen domestic production of the pulse and further reduce import dependence and keep prices under control. The Department of Consumer Affairs is identifying rainfed areas that can be brought under chana cultivation, two people aware of the matter said. It has identified 80 districts across states, including Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab, Jharkhand and Bihar, where rainfed land could be utilised to grow the crop, the people said. India imported gram worth $3.63 billion in FY26, down from a record $5.54 billion in FY25. The proposed move aims to build on this reduction by expanding domestic chana supplies. “The government has a tentative estimate of around 2.38 million hectares of rainfed land across watershed areas in the identified states, and the exact extent of land suitable for chana cultivation will be mapped by the two departments,” said the first among the two officials cited above. "As part of the plan, the department will approach the agriculture ministry and the Department of Land Resources to identify suitable acreage and assess its additional production potential,” the official added. The department plans to support farmers with quality seeds and technical assistance, along with procurement assurance, the second official said. Chana is a relatively less water-intensive crop that can be grown using residual soil moisture after the kharif harvest. The government expects the proposed expansion to strengthen domestic supplies and eventually create scope for chana dal exports, subject to domestic demand and surplus availability. 2c176b9bf28da1a6.title: State govt. employees who donate organs likely to get leave for recuperation
2c176b9bf28da1a6.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 01:15 am IST - CHENNAI Health Minister K.G. Arunraj speaking at an event organised by Gleneagles Hospital in Chennai on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: J. Johan Sathyadas Health Minister K.G. Arunraj on Tuesday said that the State government was likely to provide 42 days of leave to employees who donate organs. Similarly, if organ donors themselves need organs, their needs will be prioritised. Speaking at an event to honour over 250 living donor liver transplantation journeys, supported by the Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme at Gleneagles Hospital, he said that government hospitals too will soon take up live liver organ transplants in a transparent manner. Dr. Arunraj urged the public to take care of their liver health. He said that those who are used to consuming alcohol every day should gradually reduce the quantum and take to responsible drinking. A. Aravind, Director of Medical Education, said that the cost of one live liver transplant was around ₹22 lakh and it was great that the State government was making it possible through insurance. Joy Varghese, director of Hepatology, Gleneagles, said that over 100 beneficiaries of live liver transplant were children between the ages of 5 and 14. Many of them had been referred from the government-run hospitals, he said, adding that the hospital was indebted to doctors in government hospitals for the trust they placed in them. Sholinganallur MLA P. Saravanan, S. Niranjani, chief operating officer, and J. Sophia Ansetta, medical director were present. 4459a04203b498ad.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 01:34 am IST - NEW DELHI Indian women’s hockey goalkeeper Savita Punia. File | Photo Credit: PTI Veteran goalkeeper Savita Punia has been rested from the Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal, replaced by Bansari Solanki in the Indian women's hockey squad unveiled on Tuesday, with head coach Sjoerd Marijne also announcing changes to the roles of some players during the event. The tournament is scheduled to be held from November 19 to 28 at the newly-built International Sports Complex, Nathu Barkheda, Bhopal and India will enter as the defending champions. India will begin their campaign against Malaysia on the opening day of the competition. Mid-fielder Salima Tete will continue to lead the team, which is playing its first international tournament after the historic gold medal at the Asian Games in Japan last month. The hosts have secured the ACT title in 2016, 2023 and 2024. The six-team competition will feature India, China, Japan, Malaysia, Thailand and South Korea. Like India, South Korea too have won the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy three times. The 25-year-old Bansari has been part of the squad that won the Asia Cup last year. Bichu Devi Kharibam retained her place as the other custodian in the squad. "This is the moment I want to give other players the chance to showcase their talent on the international stage. Some players will be playing in different positions than they normally do, so that I can see how they perform in a different role," said Marijne. "We are excited to play in front of the home crowd and finish the year well," he added. As part of the role shuffling, Rutuja Dadaso Pisal, who played as a forward in the Asian Games, has been named in the mid-field for the ACT. Similarly, mid-fielder Nikki Pradhan is part of the defensive line-up, while Ishika Chaudhary has been moved from defence to mid-field. f48a08324b837576.title: A hundred years ago | A case under the Companies Act
f48a08324b837576.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 02:26 am IST Bombay, November 10: Mr. P.D. Shamdasani, a shareholder of the Tata Iron and Steel Company and a most persistent critic of the Tata House, has for once succeeded in putting seven of the Steel Company’s Directors in the wrong though he has in almost every shareholders’ meeting of the company threatened them with prosecution on many allegations of mismanagement. The present case against Sri Dorab Tata, Sir Cowasji Jehangir, Narottam Morarji, Sir Phiroze Sethna, Mr. N.B. Saklatwala, Mr. F.E. Dinshaw and Sir Ibrahim Rabintulla Tata Sons Ltd and others is that they failed to comply with the provisions of the Indian Companies Act in not having convened the Company’s annual general meeting within fifteen months of the preceding meeting. The accused, in pleading guilty, urged that this was a fit case for warning and discharge. The Magistrate expressed inability to do so as this was a case under the Indian Companies Act and not one under the Penal Code. He convicted and fined them to a pay a fine of Rs. 5 each. cca4b5e6e501b12d.title: Kin of three workers who died at private firm in Hosur agree to receive bodies
cca4b5e6e501b12d.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 12:37 am IST - SALEM A day after three men allegedly died of asphyxiation on the premises of Tata Marigold Company (a unit of Tata Electronics) in Hosur, their relatives agreed to receive their bodies on Tuesday. Acknowledging the tragedy, Nalco Water, in a statement, said: “We are deeply saddened by the tragic incident that resulted in the deaths of three workers engaged by a sub-contractor of Nalco Water, an Ecolab company, at the Tata Electronics site. This incident occurred in a utility facility, operated by Nalco Water. We are working with the local authorities in the investigation of this incident.” On Monday evening, contract workers B. Akmal, 28, of Panchapalli and M. Sarathi Kumar, 28, of Thirumalvadi in Dharmapuri district; and Kaveri, 30, of Hosur in Krishnagiri district had carried out maintenance and cleaning work inside the nano-filtration feed tank at the factory in Vanniyapuram. At the time, the three experienced difficulty breathing and collapsed. They were rushed to a private hospital but died on the way. On Tuesday, relatives of the deceased tried to stage a road roko outside the Krishnagiri Government Medical College Hospital, where the three bodies were being kept, to demand compensation for the deaths. The police restrained them. Subsequently, the sub-contractor conducted talks with the relatives in the presence of District Superintendent of Police G.S. Anitha and assured them a solatium of ₹30 lakh each apart from the insurance amount. Based on the assurance, the relative agreed to receive the bodies after a post-mortem. Nalco Water said, “Our first priority is to extend all possible support to the families. Safety is a core value and is fundamental to everything we do at Ecolab. We take this incident extremely seriously. We are deeply committed to upholding the highest standards of safety across our operations and the sites where we work.” Published - November 11, 2026 12:37 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutio

The celebrations began with a palanquin procession of the deities from the temple to the goshala , where the cows were worshipped. Niskinchana Bhakta Dasa, president of the Hare Krishna Movement, Visakhapatnam, spoke about the significance of Lord Krishna’s G ovardhan Leela a nd G au puja. They also performed govardhan parikrama (walking around) the offering. The programme included damodara aarti and the offering of ghee lamps to the deity. The celebrations concluded with the distribution of prasadam . 73c1d076fc4d4ad0.title: Fear, stigma, financial concerns keep cancer patients from seeking timely care, says expert
73c1d076fc4d4ad0.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 11:52 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Dr Rupali Basu, senior vice president, regional business head - East and Andhra Pradesh, HCG Cancer Centre, during an interaction with The Hindu in Visakhapatnam on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: V RAJU Early diagnosis of cancer, coupled with timely intervention and access to appropriate treatment, is crucial to improving survival rates and in helping patients lead a better quality of life, said Rupali Basu, senior vice president, regional business head - East and Andhra Pradesh, HCG Cancer Centre. Emphasising the need to strengthen cancer awareness and screening, Ms. Basu said that many patients continued to approach hospitals only at an advanced stage of the disease owing to fear, social stigma, lack of awareness of early symptoms, financial concerns and geographical barriers to accessing specialised healthcare. Stronger community-level awareness programmes and accessible screening facilities could play a significant role in changing this trend, she said. Speaking to The Hindu , she said that cancer was increasingly emerging as a concern across age groups and communities, with several factors, including an ageing population, tobacco consumption, cigarette smoking, changing lifestyles and environmental exposure, contributing to the growing burden. While breast cancer remained a major concern among women, lung and colorectal cancers were among the commonly diagnosed cancers in men. Brain tumours and other forms of cancer also required greater awareness and timely medical attention. Ms. Basu stressed that cancer treatment required more than just identifying the disease. A multidisciplinary approach, involving tumour boards, was essential to determine the most appropriate course of treatment for each patient. Accurate diagnosis, the latest medical technology and coordinated care could make a significant difference to treatment outcomes and the patient’s overall experience. 32e378b7558b4e37.title: The War Putin Wanted to Keep Away Is Coming Home to Russia
32e378b7558b4e37.summary: Olga was jolted awake by an explosion so powerful that her apartment building shuddered and the windows and furniture shook. Looking outside, she saw a plume of thick black smoke rising from a military equipment factory that had just been hit by a missile. Residents panicked, said Olga, a 49-year-old choreographer. “We didn’t know whether we should run to a shelter,” she said. The strike on the plant left six people dead and another 26 injured, according to the local governor. Olga doesn’t live in Kyiv, Kherson or any other Ukrainian city that’s been pounded for years by President Vladimir Putin’s forces. This is Kirov, a Russian city about 800 kilometers northeast of Moscow known for its 16th century onion-domed monastery rather than being in a war zone. The missile strike was one of the many that have inflicted rising civilian casualties inside Russia in recent months. They are bringing Putin’s war home to his own people after he promised a swift and glorious victory. Since Ukrainian strikes intensified in mid-summer, people inside Russia are killed almost every week, according to a Bloomberg analysis of statements from regional authorities on their Telegram channels. Meanwhile, as Russia prepared to resume trilateral negotiations with the US and Ukraine on a potential peace deal in Abu Dhabi this week, confidential data hacked from Russia’s statistics service showed about 400,000 of its people have been killed fighting in Ukraine. It’s a scale of military deaths the country hasn’t seen since World War II. The Kremlin tightly controls the narrative around the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, now nine months into its fifth year. While the death toll touches a huge number of families in Russia, it won’t necessarily have political consequences for Putin, who taps into historical memory to justify the sacrifice in what he claims is an existential fight with the West in Ukraine. ee4a7dd1e82b3913.title: Delhi: CPCB mulls raising monitoring cap after readings go blank
ee4a7dd1e82b3913.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 05:30 am IST - New Delhi Delhi’s air quality improved to the ‘poor’ category on Tuesday, with the 24-hour average AQI recorded at 299, just below the ‘very poor’ threshold of 300. | Photo Credit: ANI The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) on Tuesday indicated that it was considering steps to capture peak levels of particulate matter (PM), a major pollutant, that exceed the existing monitoring range, after air quality data from several government monitoring stations in Delhi went missing for hours during the pollution spike following Deepavali on Sunday. The Hindu reported on Monday that the data gaps had led to an artificially lower official air quality index (AQI), making air quality appear better than it actually was, according to experts. In a statement on Tuesday, the CPCB said PM levels were measured only up to 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre (µg/m³) for AQI calculations, which explained the missing data on Deepavali night, when actual concentrations exceeded this limit. “The PM analysers deployed at the time of introduction of the NAQI (National Air Quality Index) [in 2015] were calibrated for a measurement range of 0-1,000 µg/m³. Accordingly, consistent with this, the designed system of automated data validation treats hourly readings beyond the calibrated range as outside range, and such readings are not used in the computation,” the CPCB statement read. “During extreme episodes, which are occasional, like Diwali firecracker bursting, this may appear as a data gap at the particular station concerned, and those hours do not contribute to the 24-hour average of the relevant pollutant for the concerned station,” the statement added. The CPCB said internal deliberations and consultations on processing data “beyond system design range” were under way. 259f3a995c68bcd1.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 12:15 am IST - Chennai Tasmac headquarters will classify every shop as an A, B and C shop on the basis of its average daily sales and accordingly deploy workforce. (File) | Photo Credit: B. VELANKANNI RAJ The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) is set to reshuffle employees across its retail network in Tamil Nadu, deploying staff at outlets based on manpower requirements. 75e338a3dfe88607.title: India A-New Zealand A series ends in draw after rain washes out fourth day of third unofficial Test
75e338a3dfe88607.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 01:14 am IST - LINCOLN, NEW ZEALAND The third and final unofficial Test between India A and New Zealand A ended in a draw, with the series ending in a draw. All three four-day matches failed to produce a result. At the end of day 4, NZ A was 36/2, with Dean Foxcroft (10*) and Zak Gibson (1*) unbeaten. They trailed by 428 runs. Earlier, New Zealand A won the toss and elected to field first. A 175-run opening stand between Yashasvi Jaiswal (102 in 138 balls, with 16 fours and two sixes) and Sai Sudharsan (88 in 215 balls, with 11 fours) started off things for India. Half-centuries came from the bat of Tilak Varma (81 in 164 balls, with five fours and two sixes), skipper Dhruv Jurel (71 in 95 balls, with nine fours and two sixes) and Washington Sundar (50* in 107 balls, with two fours) as India posted 464/5. Zak Gibson (2/73) was the leading wicket-taker for NZ. India’s batting was a big plus ahead of the Test series starting on November 19, with Devdutt Padikkal (326 runs in three matches and five innings at an average of 65.20, with a century and a fifty) being the top run-scorer. After a few poor scores, Yashasvi Jaiswal (279 runs in three matches and five innings at an average of 69.75, with two centuries) also scored back-to-back tons. Sai Sudharsan (231 runs in three matches and five innings at an average of 46.20, with two fifties) and skipper Jurel (179 runs in three matches and four innings at an average of 44.75, with a century and a fifty) also played some fine knocks for India. Uncapped batter Yash Rathod (223 runs in two matches at an average of 111.50, with a century and a fifty) also was a big positive for India. Auqib Nabi (six wickets in a match) and Mohammed Siraj (four wickets in a match) were the leading wicket-takers for India. India Test squad for two NZ Tests: Shubman Gill [C], Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul [VC], Devdutt Padikkal, Rishabh Pant [WK]*, Dhruv Jurel [WK], Ravindra Jadeja, Anshul Kamboj, Jasprit Bumrah, Pras

db5df5e4f7a3cce5.title: Around 150 persons treated for cracker-related burns in Vellore, nearby districts
db5df5e4f7a3cce5.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 11:55 pm IST - VELLORE Sanitary workers remove cracker wastes in Vellore Corporation. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Around 150 persons received treatment for cracker-related burns at various healthcare centres, government hospitals in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts. Health officials said that the Government Medical College and Hospital in Vellore and Tiruvannamalai treated 22 and 35 persons respectively for cracker-related burns. “Most of the victims were treated as out-patients. They were below the age of 15. A team of health officials was deployed for the purpose,” said Edvina Vasantha, dean, Government Medical College Hospital in Tiruvannamalai. In Tirupattur district, on an average, 10-12 cases of burns were reported at the Government Taluk Hospital at Tirupattur, Vaniyambadi, Ambur, and Natrampalli towns each, during the festival. The government health centres in Jawadhu Hills also reported at least 15 burn cases over three days (November 7-9). “No major burns were reported within Vellore town during the festival. Adequate medical teams were in place to attend to emergencies,” P. Pratap Kumar, City Health Officer (CHO), Vellore Corporation, told The Hindu . In Ranipet district, more than 40 cases of burns were reported in government hospitals at Arakkonam, Walajah, Arcot, Ranipet, and Sholinghur towns during the festival. Health officials said that private hospitals and clinics also reported cases of cracker-related burns. Most of the persons are treated as out-patients in these districts. A large volume of cracker waste was generated in these districts. Around 550 tonnes of cracker wastes were generated in Vellore and Tiruvannamalai Corporation on November 8-9. More than 500 sanitary workers were roped in for the purpose. Most of the wastes include paper, cardboard, half-burnt, and unused crackers that are mostly dumped on roads and streets. These were sent to micro compost centres for recycling.

fe2151dac5c26ccb.title: No plans to switch federations as of now: Abhimanyu
fe2151dac5c26ccb.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 11:55 pm IST - Budapest Abhimanya Mishra. | Photo Credit: File photo: SUDHAKARA JAIN American Grandmaster Abhimanyu Mishra said he has no current plans to switch federations, explaining that his earlier comments referred to a hypothetical situation. “Actually, this was a huge miscommunication. Essentially, as of now, I don’t want to switch federations at all,” Abhimanyu told The Hindu on the sidelines of the Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot here. He said his response to that hypothetical question was that he might consider a switch. “But the thing is, this does not mean that I’m searching to change federation at all currently,” he said. Abhimanyu also spoke about playing simultaneous exhibitions to help cover expenses. The sessions, which involved taking on several opponents and could last hours, provided some income but were tiring. “And I was getting some money out of that, which was helping a bit,” he said. In Budapest, Abhimanyu has been drawn in Group C alongside Magnus Carlsen, Anish Giri, Ian Nepomniachtchi, Haik M. Martirosyan and Shakhriyar Mamedyarov. He will face each opponent twice in the Fast Classic group stage. The 24-player event combines blitz, rapid and Fast Classic, with players tested at all three speeds in the knockouts. The chance to play Carlsen twice was particularly appealing, with Abhimanyu describing it as a source of joy and a learning experience. TThe strength of the field had convinced him to accept the invitation. “I mean, saying no to a tournament like this is a bit ridiculous, honestly,” he said. bcef827141be2997.title: Two persons killed in separate road incidents
bcef827141be2997.summary: Updated - November 10, 2026 11:48 pm IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI Two persons were killed in separate road incidents near Kilpennathur and Arcot towns in Tiruvannamalai and Ranipet districts respectively on Tuesday. The police identified the victims as V. Nandakumar, 45, and T. Venkatesan, 35. Initial inquiry revealed that Nandakumar, a private school staff, was on his way to school on the Chennai – Bengaluru Highway (NH 48) when a private bus hit the two-wheeler he was riding at Melvisharam in Ranipet. Passersby rushed a badly injured Nandakumar to Government Taluk Hospital in Arcot town, where doctors said that he was brought dead. A case was registered and a probe is under way. In a separate incident, the victim, Venkatesan was riding his autorickshaw from a petrol pump towards the Chittoor – Cuddalore Highway at Kilpennathur, when a car rammed the autorickshaw. The police said in the impact, Venkatesan died on the spot. On being informed, Kilpennathur police inspected the spot and a case was registered. Special teams were formed to nab the car driver, and a probe is under way. 65337055769d5a1d.title: Fifty years ago | Foreign intelligence agents at work in U.S.
65337055769d5a1d.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 02:44 am IST Washington, November 10: Either with or without the knowledge of the U.S. Government, a number of foreign intelligence organisations appear to have established a regular presence in the United States, and have been engaged in activities which are for the most part illegal. The most publicised case to-date is that of the South Korean Intelligence Agency (KCIA), which has been accused of not only spying on South Korean and American nationals in the U.S., but also of giving huge bribes to U.S. Congressmen and others in a bid to influence U.S. defence and foreign policies — former Defence Secretary Melvin Laird has now disclosed that in 1970 the South Korean “lobby” tried to undermine the Nixon Administration’s decision to withdraw 20,000 American troops from South Korea. The Geneva-based council regularly examines the rights records of all 193 UN member states - generally about every four to five years - as part of a process known as the universal periodic review.
