4f4a1af698b44ae6.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
4f4a1af698b44ae6.summary: Updated - November 11, 2026 01:13 am IST If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues. In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. d83b333384396245.title: IND vs NZ 3rd ODI abandoned due to rain, India retains 2-0 series lead
d83b333384396245.summary: Rain played spoilsport as the third ODI between New Zealand and India at Seddon Park here on Tuesday was called off. India lead the five-match series 2-0 as the two teams head to Tauranga for the final two games, scheduled for November 13 and 15. India skipper Shubman Gill won the toss for the third time in a row and opted to bowl, fielding an unchanged side from the previous two games. However, just as the covers were coming off for a 40-overs-a-side contest, the heavens opened up once again. With at least 70 minutes remaining before the local cut-off time of 7:50 pm for a 20-overs-a-side game, the two umpires decided to call off the match. The weather forecast for this game had always been gloomy, with a 90 per cent chance of rain predicted throughout the day. This was supposed to be the last game of the series for skipper Shubman Gill and senior wicketkeeper KL Rahul before they link up with the Test squad in Wellington. They will be accompanied by Kuldeep Yadav, Anshul Kamboj

df9643ca6bc5a6bb.title: U.K. writer M. John Harrison wins Booker for AI-tinged apocalyptic novel
df9643ca6bc5a6bb.summary: Updated - November 10, 2026 08:15 am IST - LONDON M. John Harrison, author of "The End of Everything" holds the trophy for winning the Booker Prize during the Booker Prize 2026 ceremony at Old Billingsgate in London, November 10, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP U.K. author M. John Harrison won the Booker Prize on Monday (November 9, 2026) for his enigmatic novel "The End of Everything", which echoes concerns about artificial intelligence in a darkly satirical depiction of post-apocalyptic Britain. Mr. Harrison, 81, became the oldest winner of the award, which comes with a £50,000 ($67,000) prize and a boost in sales and profile for the winner. Review | ‘The End of Everything’ by M. John Harrison: the aliens are here A veteran of the British science fiction literary scene, it was Mr. Harrison’s first time being shortlisted for the coveted prize, which critics have said was long overdue. He beat shortlisted authors Marlon James, Douglas Stuart, Elizabeth Strout, Luke Kennard and Rebecca Perry, whose entries ranged from a queer epic unfolding in 1980s Kingston to a campus satire set in modern-day London. "The End of Everything" came out "ahead in terms of both its extraordinary expert writing, but also huge ambition," chair of the judges Mary Beard told a press conference. Mr. Harrison's 13th novel follows the beachcomber Phillip Tennent and his dementia-stricken, free-spirited aunt Marnie, set in the near-future on the windswept English coast invaded by mysterious objects known as the iGhetti. An unnamed catastrophe plunges the characters into a murky post-apocalyptic world where the European continent seems to have disappeared and the arrival of the iGhetti, which can imitate humans, evoke interactions with artificial intelligence. "One main point of the book is that if, or when, such an apocalypse comes it will be incomprehensible," Ms. Beard said, adding the book spoke to the present "moment". 7f3ebff4cc6a832e.title: Five persons, including four girls, drown in irrigation tank in Tiruvannamalai
7f3ebff4cc6a832e.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 12:20 am IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI Collector Vandhana Garg and Superintendent of Police R. Uthayakumar during their inspection of the irrigation tank on Monday. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement A staff nurse and four girls of a government-recognised children’s home for girls drowned in an irrigation tank at Samuthiram village here on Monday (November 9, 2026). The deceased were identified as staff nurse Thenmozhi, 24, Vijayalakshmi, 14, Alli, 14, Poomika, 13, and Valliammal, 16. Except Valliammal, who belongs to Kilpennathur village, the other three girls are siblings from Karapattu village near Chengam. The deceased did not know swimming, the police said. Initial inquiry revealed the home had been functioning for over a decade in the area. On Monday afternoon, Thenmozhi, along with around 13 girls, went to the irrigation tank on Perumbakkam Main Road to bathe. Poomika and her siblings and Valliammal stepped into the water and slipped and fell into a deeper portion of the irrigation tank. The police said Thenmozhi tried to save the children but also drowned. Hearing the other girls’ shouts, the area’s residents rushed to the spot and alerted the Tiruvannamalai West police and firefighters. Firefighters retrieved the bodies and sent them to the Government Medical College and Hospital in Tiruvannamalai town for a post-mortem. A case has been registered. Collector Vandhana Garg and Superintendent of Police R. Uthayakumar met the families of the deceased at the hospital in the presence of hospital dean Edvina Vasantah and inspected the irrigation tank. A probe is under way. The deceased were identified as staff nurse Thenmozhi, 24, Vijayalakshmi, 14, Alli, 14, Poomika, 13, and Valliammal, 16. Except Valliammal, who belongs to Kilpennathur village, the other three girls are siblings from Karapattu village near Chengam. The deceased did not know swimming, the police said. Initial inquiry revealed the home had been functioning for over a decade in the area. On Monday afternoon, Thenmozhi, along with around 13 girls, went to the irrigation tank on Perumbakkam Main Road to bathe. Poomika and her siblings and Valliammal stepped into the water and slipped and fell into a deeper portion of the irrigation tank. The police said Thenmozhi tried to save the children but also drowned. Hearing the other girls’ shouts, the area’s residents rushed to the spot and alerted the Tiruvannamalai West police and firefighters. Firefighters retrieved the bodies and sent them to the Government Medical College and Hospital in Tiruvannamalai town for a post-mortem. A case has been registered. Collector Vandhana Garg and Superintendent of Police R. Uthayakumar met the families of the deceased at the hospital in the presence of hospital dean Edvina Vasantah and inspected the irrigation tank. A probe is under way. 12f72c3e816cf159.title: WTA Chennai Open: Postponement of singles final sparks controversy
12f72c3e816cf159.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 12:11 am IST - CHENNAI The postponement of the WTA 250 Chennai Open singles final due to rain and fireworks-induced smog on Sunday evening sparked controversy over the organisers’ handling of the situation. The final, set for a 6:30 p.m. start, was delayed thrice due to rain. Once the rain relented for good, the organisers dried the centre court at the SDAT stadium and rescheduled the final at 9 p.m. However, the smog caused by the Deepavali firecrackers had made the air quality hazardous and the match had to be shifted to 11 a.m. on Monday in which Poland’s Magda Linette defeated Indonesia’s Janice Tjen, the reigning champion, in three sets. Christopher Bint, Tjen’s coach, in an Instagram story late on Sunday night, claimed that the organisers wanted to conduct the final despite the extremely poor air quality. “And they still wanted the match to go ahead,” he wrote, attaching a screenshot showing an AQI of 1556 in Chennai. Later, after Monday’s summit clash, Bint said, “Maybe, it could have just been postponed a little bit earlier.” Linette felt the doubles final, which started at 4 p.m. on Sunday, could have been moved forward. “We should have put the doubles final way earlier which would have given us a lot of time,” said the 34-year-old Pole. Hiten Joshi, the tournament director, said, “In these emergencies, the tournament supervisor (Sheetal Iyer) has to get permission from the WTA. So, they were going back and forth, and she also wanted to wait to see if any play was possible.” Published - November 10, 2026 12:11 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 40a90eb64af97d91.title: APSDRF rescues eight, evacuates 341 during Cyclone Arnab relief efforts
40a90eb64af97d91.summary: Updated - November 10, 2026 12:20 am IST - VIJAYAWADA DGP Harish Kumar Gupta presenting rewards to the APSDRF personnel at the AP Police Headquarters in Mangalagiri on Monday. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response Force (APSDRF) shifted 341 people to safe places, rescued eight, and retrieved a body during Cyclone Arnab. Inspector General of Police (IGP-Operations) Ch. Srikanth, along with senior officers of Andhra Pradesh Special Police (APSP) met Director General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta at the Police Headquarters at Mangalagiri on Monday (November 9, 2026), and explained the operations taken up by APSDRF during the calamity. The SDRF officials explained that eleven special teams comprising 328 officers and personnel rendered services in the State from October 27 to November 1. Rescue and relief operations were carried out in Bapatla, Konaseema, Kakinada, Srikakulam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, West Godavari, East Godavari, Polavaram, and Anakapalli districts. A total of 728 fallen trees were cleared, road clearance operations were taken up at 58 locations, and 31 electricity poles that fell on roads were removed, facilitating the movement of emergency vehicles, Mr. Srikanth said. The ‘Dial 112’ State Control Room played a crucial role in providing assistance to the people trapped in cyclone. In three days, the control room staff received 369 cyclone-related emergency calls from 17 districts. The SDRF, with the coordination of Dial-112 rescued 40 passengers travelling in a bus stranded in floodwaters in Srikakulam. In another incident, the personnel assisted in rescuing eight fishermen caught in danger due to the cyclone, the officers said. The DGP appreciated the courage, dedication, and commitment of the APSDRF in saving the lives of people during disasters, stating that their services are a matter of pride for the Police Department. He presented rewards to officers and personnel who exhibited outstanding bravery in rescue

fc50fb31451033a0.title: Diwali 2026: Global leaders – Anthony Albanese, Emmanuel Macron, Mark Carney – call for unity, peace, prosperity
fc50fb31451033a0.summary: Wishing peace, prosperity, and hope, world leaders—including Emmanuel Macron, Anthony Albanese, and Mark Carney—shared their Diwali greetings on Sunday with all those celebrating the festival of lights. Albanese said Diwali was “the great celebration of the victory of light,” bringing communities together across religious and cultural boundaries. “We can all take pride and joy in just how intrinsically Diwali has become part of the face of modern Australia,” he said in a video message, noting that the signs and symbols of Diwali carry a message that speaks beyond religion or culture. Anthony Albanese, Emmanuel Macron and Mark Carney were among the leaders who sent greetings. Messages also came from leaders in Sri Lanka, the UAE, Pakistan, Israel, Malaysia and the Seychelles. Albanese described Diwali as a celebration of light that brings communities together across religious and cultural boundaries. He said its message calls for compassion, understanding, love and unity. Macron wished people unity, peace and hope, while Carney highlighted Diwali’s symbolism: light over darkness, good over evil and knowledge over ignorance. In Bangkok, Thailand’s prime minister inaugurated the Amazing Thailand Grand Diwali Festival, a 27-day event. In the United States, Donald Trump marked the occasion by lighting a diya at the White House. Gautam Gambhir, Jay Shah, the BCCI, former cricketers and IPL teams shared festive messages. Their wishes emphasized peace, prosperity, family, togetherness and hope. “It is a call to compassion and understanding, and of love and unity,” he said. “Wishing all my Indian friends in India, France, and around the world, a very happy Diwali! May its light inspire us to ever uphold unity, peace, and hope!” Macron wrote on social media, alongside a similar message in Hindi. Carney said communities across Canada were joining millions around the world to celebrate Diwali, the Festival of Lights — marking the triumph of light over darkness, good over evil,

6824daa35caf6638.title: Fifty years ago | Power struggle in China had begun 2 years ago
6824daa35caf6638.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 02:26 am IST Tokyo, November 9: Though the ouster from power of the four Shanghai radicals, led by Mao Tse-tung’s widow, Chiang Ching, became known to the outside world only last month, an acute power struggle within the Chinese Communist Party had been going on for nearly two years with Chairman Mao himself ranged against the gang of four, as they have now come to be known. Some light on this hitherto hidden aspect has been thrown by an editorial carried by the Liberation Army Daily, official organ of the People’s Liberation Army. According to the editorial, the gang of four had been engaging over a period of time in an attempt to usurp top party and State leadership. Mao, however, saw through the plot and made it impossible for their schemes to be achieved. 766d5dd61af4ec7c.title: Optional Travel Insurance Scheme urged for railway staff
766d5dd61af4ec7c.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 12:24 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Senior National Railway Trade Union leader and Divisional Railway Users’ Consultative Committee (DRUCC) member Chalasani Gandhi on Tuesday urged the Railway Board to extend the Optional Travel Insurance Scheme (OTIS) to serving railway employees, pensioners, and their eligible family members travelling on Privilege Passes and Privilege Ticket Orders (PTOs). Mr. Gandhi stated in a release that following directions from the Supreme Court the Railway Board had extended the optional travel insurance facility – previously restricted to online ticket bookings – to passengers purchasing reserved tickets through Railway Passenger Reservation System (PRS) counters with effect from October 27. Under the scheme, passengers receive an accident insurance coverage of up to ₹10 lakh against a nominal premium of 45 paise. The scheme covers compensation for death, permanent disability, hospitalisation expenses, and transportation of mortal remains. Questioning the rationale behind excluding railway personnel from the welfare measure, Mr. Gandhi stressed that railway employees face constant risks while rendering dedicated service. Extending the insurance protection to employees and their families booking tickets online or via PRS counters on Passes and PTOs would benefit lakhs of railway families nationwide. He urged the Railway Board to issue necessary policy amendments allowing staff and their dependents to opt for the insurance by paying the standard premium, while establishing clear guidelines for policy issuance and claim settlements. ca4cec0548bff88f.title: Trump, in CBS interview, says deportation policy was ‘too tough’
ca4cec0548bff88f.summary: Published - November 09, 2026 04:52 am IST - WASHINGTON U.S. President Donald Trump. | Photo Credit: AP U.S. President Donald Trump said that his mass deportation of undocumented immigrants was "too tough," according to an excerpt of an interview with CBS aired on Sunday (November 8, 2026). Asked about his deportation policy, Mr. Trump told CBS ' "60 Minutes": "I think it was too tough...I think it might be too tough." The excerpt was published by CBS on X ahead of a broadcast of the interview on network TV later on Sunday (November 8, 2026). It was recorded after the Republican Party's heavy loss in midterm elections on Tuesday. While Mr. Trump has won some domestic support for securing the U.S. southern border, his administration's aggressive push to deport millions of undocumented migrants has drawn widespread criticism. However, Mr. Trump on Friday (November 6, 2026) appointed the architect of that hardline policy, Stephen Miller, as his chief of staff, signalling a bare-knuckle fightback after the Republican election loss. Mr. Miller has been synonymous with scenes of masked immigration agents committing violence after he backed federal agents who shot and killed two Americans early this year. This opening marks the subsidiary's first physical expansion beyond California, with its US branches now at eight locations. The inauguration ceremony was led by SBI Group Chairman Challa Sreenivasulu Setty, alongside Consul General of India in Houston, DC Manjunath and Frisco Mayor Mark Hill. ea705bc56d367b72.title: Bullion may remain under pressure as markets track US-Iran war, inflation
ea705bc56d367b72.summary: Bullion prices are likely to remain under pressure next week as investors track developments in the US-Iran conflict, movements in crude oil prices and inflation data for cues on the outlook for interest rates, analysts said. The focus will be on inflation prints from China, the US, Germany, Japan and India. Investors will also closely track speeches by Federal Reserve officials and US employment data. Chinese economic indicators will be important for industrial metals, they added. Geopolitical developments will remain a key driver after US President Donald Trump confirmed fresh military strikes on Iran, while claiming that Washington had made "a lot of progress" in negotiations with Tehran, adding another layer of uncertainty. The domestic commodities market will remain closed during the morning session on Tuesday due to Diwali-Balipratipada. Three people who were also injured in the blaze on Friday (November 6, 2026) are undergoing treatment in a critical condition. All the victims were employees of Spectron Engineering Private Limited, a Mumbai-based company engaged by OIL. One person was killed in the fire on the day of the incident, while two died the next day. A mechanical helper, Sailen Gogoi, who was undergoing treatment at a private hospital here, died during the day, taking the toll to four, the official said. A fire had broken out on November 6 after an explosion during maintenance work at OIL's intermediate tank farm (ITF) in Tengakhat, the public sector undertaking said in a statement. An ITF is a facility where petroleum products are temporarily stored in tanks before being transferred for further processing or transportation. Meanwhile, OIL has instituted a high-level inquiry to probe into the incident, another official said. The committee has put all four OIL employees who were in-charge of the ITF, including three officers, on suspension, he said. "They were placed under suspension until the investigation is over," the official added. Credit: X/@ChessbaseIndia Anuj Shrivatri on Sunday (November 8, 2026) became India’s 100th chess Grandmaster, by winning the 7th ASEAN+ Individual Open chess championship in Ozamiz City, the Philippines. The 22-year-old Anuj also became the first GM from Madhya Pradesh. He won the tournament with seven points from nine rounds after suffering a loss in the opening round. His triumph enabled him earn the GM title. The legendary Viswanathan Anand had become the country’s first Grandmaster in 1988. The wait for the 100th GM was watched intently after S. Aswath and V.S. 4f440a6990bb54de.title: NGT issues notice to Tirunelveli Collector over threats to Tamirabharani fish species
4f440a6990bb54de.summary: Updated - November 08, 2026 07:06 pm IST - CHENNAI Some of the fishes found in the Tamirabharani River in Tirunelveli district. File | Photo Credit: Special arrangement The Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal (NGT), New Delhi, has issued notice to the Tirunelveli Collector and five others over threats faced by fish species in Tamirabharani River due to pollution and habitat loss. Taking suo motu cognisance of a report, titled ‘Tamirabharani’s Endemic Fish Face Threats From Pollution, Habitat Loss’, published in The Hindu on September 28, the Bench, comprising Justice Arun Kumar Tyagi and expert members A. Senthil Vel and Afroz Ahamed, directed that the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board, the Central Pollution Control Board’s Regional Office in Chennai, Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE), and Agasthyamalai Community Conservation Centre (ACCC) be impleaded as respondents, besides the Collector. The order said: “The above news item attracts the provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and prima facie raises substantial questions relating to the environment arising out of the implementation of the enactments specified in Schedule I to the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.” The Bench directed the Registry to list the matter before the Southern Bench of the Tribunal, Chennai, on January 22, 2027, as the cause of action had arisen within its territorial jurisdiction. It also directed the respondents to file their responses before the Bench at least one day ahead of the date of hearing. The Hindu had reported that 125 fish species had been identified in upstream, midstream and lower estuarine stretches of the river. Seven of them are endemic to the Tamirabharani. f1fb36e5c6e7e558.title: Congress donations fall nearly 75%, sharpest decline in a decade
f1fb36e5c6e7e558.summary: The Congress party's receipts from donations above Rs 20,000 plunged nearly 75 per cent to Rs 130.69 crore in 2025-26, the steepest annual fall in such contributions in a decade, an analysis of the party's filings with the Election Commission shows. The party had received Rs 517.39 crore in such contributions in 2024-25, according to its 2024-25 contribution report submitted to the commission. A comparison with the preceding 12 financial years shows that the last steeper fall was in 2015-16, when Congress' disclosed donations dropped roughly 86 per cent from Rs 141.46 crore the previous year. The latest decline follows two years of higher collections. Congress received Rs 281.48 crore in disclosed donations in 2023-24, rising to Rs 517.39 crore in 2024-25, the year Lok Sabha elections were held. 4eaa140d0d65a62f.title: Hacked Records Show 400,000 Russians Killed in War on Ukraine
4eaa140d0d65a62f.summary: Russia has recorded the deaths of about 400,000 of its people fighting in Ukraine since the full-scale invasion almost five years ago, according to confidential data held by the country’s statistics agency, Rosstat.
4eaa140d0d65a62f.headline_en: Hacked Records Show 400,000 Russians Killed in War on Ukraine
4eaa140d0d65a62f.raw_facts: Russia has recorded the deaths of about 400,000 of its people fighting in Ukraine since the full-scale invasion almost five years ago, according to confidential data held by the country’s statistics agency, Rosstat.
flags: Timeline inconsistency: The full-scale invasion began in February 2022. As of mid-2024, it has been approximately two years, not 'almost five years'.

Source reliability: The claim attributes the data to 'confidential data held by Rosstat' revealed via 'hacked records'. While independent estimates (e.g., from BBC, Mediazona, or Western intelligence) have suggested Russian casualties in the hundreds of thousands, there is no verified public evidence that Rosstat's internal records were hacked and released with this specific figure.

Official vs. Independent Data: Rosstat has not officially released a figure of 400,000 deaths. Official Russian figures have historically been much lower or non-specific. Independent estimates vary widely but often fall in the range of 100,000 to 200,000+ confirmed deaths, with total casualties (including wounded) being higher. A confirmed death toll of 400,000 is on the higher end of speculative estimates and lacks a verified primary source in this context.

Unverified 'Hacked Records': Claims of hacked government statistics are common in disinformation or unverified leaks. Without a credible, independent verification of the hack and the data's authenticity, this claim is highly suspect.

484ad032df690039.title: Sonia Gandhi turned to Bhagavad Gita to resolve dilemma over politics

2a345b559a500f58.title: Amber Enterprises arm IL JIN Electronics files DRHP for ₹2,500 crore IPO
2a345b559a500f58.summary: IL JIN Electronics (India) Ltd, an arm of Amber Enterprises India Ltd, has filed preliminary papers with the market regulator Sebi to raise Rs 2,500 crore through an initial public offering (IPO). The proposed IPO is entirely a fresh issue of equity shares, with no offer for sale (OFS) component, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated November 6. The company plans to use the proceeds to repay or prepay certain outstanding borrowings, including accrued interest, availed by the company and its subsidiaries, Ascent Circuits and Shogini Technoarts. The funds will also be used to purchase plant, machinery, and equipment for its manufacturing units, as well as for general corporate purposes. 73f51ce4601d74a1.title: South Africa mourns Indian-origin TV pioneer Ramprakash Gopidayal
73f51ce4601d74a1.summary: Tributes poured in for South African Indian-origin media personality Ramprakash Gopidayal, who pioneered television programmes and radio recordings for the local Indian community, as he was cremated on Friday after succumbing to illness a day before. Popularly known as Ramu, Gopidayal, despite being an introverted, camera-shy man, started the first television programme for the Indian community, 'Impressions', on national state broadcaster South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC), in the apartheid era. He first joined the SABC as its first Indian-origin technician in 1980. With apartheid waning, the SABC started 'Impressions', a weekly magazine programme on TV for the Indian community, in 1986. It fell upon Gopidayal to take on the task of starting an unprecedented programme from scratch. Satheesan said here on Saturday (November 7) that the country’s best disaster management and resilience programme would be implemented in Keralam. He was speaking after inaugurating the valedictory session of the two-day State-level Coastal Sovereignty and Climate Resilience Conference held at the Cochin University of Science and Technology. M. Junaid Bushiri, Vice-Chancellor, presided, according to a release. Mr. Satheesan said the issues faced by fishing communities needed greater attention and effective solutions. He added that ‘Mission Samudra’ would focus on education, skill development, and employment opportunities in the maritime and fisheries sectors. Measures to address climate change, accurate disaster forecasting, early warning systems, disaster mitigation plans, and operational guidelines for disaster management will be strengthened, he said. 75a73a65a2d95bc2.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 03:38 am IST - KOLKATA The Presidency University has expelled two students for allegedly defacing Swami Vivekananda posters inside the campus, official sources said. The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad had alleged that Left student factions had vandalised the poster and had filed a police complaint on October 14. The two female students have been barred from taking admission in any course at the university in the future. The university had formed a committee to investigate the matter and has checked CCTV footage of the campus and heard from various stakeholders to come to a decision. One of them is a current student and the other was an ex-student who had finished her post-graduate course a few months back. “Two students have been expelled from the studentship/post-studentship academic activities. It has also been decided that they won’t be allowed admission to any future degree program in this university,” official sources said. “Presidency University always stood for dignified academic discourse and debate on different scientific/socio-political issues. The university is not in a position to tolerate any abuse to any thinkers/ideas/organizations,” Presidency University registrar Debajyoti Konar said. The Students’ Federation of India (SFI) condemned the expulsion on Saturday (November 7, 2026). “By imposing an expulsion that threatens to destroy the academic lives of these two students, the administration has established a deeply dangerous precedent,” their statement from the SFI Presidency unit added. 7a6420786d89b00e.title: Chennai Mayor condemns workers using bare hands to clear Deepavali waste, silt
7a6420786d89b00e.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:39 am IST - Chennai Workers clear a silt catch pit with bare hands and without protective gloves or boots in Jamalia, Perambur, amid the Northeast monsoon rains, highlighting the lack of adequate safety gear for Greater Chennai Corporation workers on November 2, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement With crackers and other Deepavali waste being cleared from streets across Chennai, conservancy workers of the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) continue to handle silt, garbage and stagnant water without adequate protective equipment, raising concerns over their safety during the Northeast monsoon. A recent report in The Hindu highlighted how workers who were engaged to clear silt from stormwater drain (SWD) catch pits and stagnant water in several parts of the city were working with bare hands, without any protective gear -- gloves and footwear. The practice was also noticed during the recent rains, where workers were seen clearing silt from a catch pit without gloves. Mayor R. Priya said the practice should not continue and pointed out that the waste generated during Deepavali, including discarded crackers, posed additional challenges for workers. “This should not be happening,” she said, adding that cracker waste could contain chemicals and required separate cleaning arrangements rather than being mixed with regular garbage. A GCC official acknowledged that the provisions made for safety equipment in the estimates were inadequate. “Invariably, sewage gets mixed with stormwater drains, whatever we may say. The provisions made in the estimates are very limited and are largely based on the number of man-days. From next time onwards, we will make more liberal provisions for safety gear and incur some additional expenditure, as it is necessary for the workers’ safety,” the official said. Noel Tata will retire as Chairman and Director of Voltas Ltd on November 11, 2026, upon attaining the age of superannuation under Tata Group governance guidelines. Following his retirement, "the Board has appointed him as Chairman Emeritus of the Company with effect from November 12, 2026," said Voltas, a Tata Group firm, in its regulatory filing. eabbfaffceff3701.title: Students urged to dream big, prepare for a self-reliant India
eabbfaffceff3701.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 11:17 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Students should dare to dream big, think independently and pursue ambitious goals to drive innovation and contribute to the vision of a self-reliant India, said Prof. Ramesh Srikonda, Director of the School of Planning and Architecture, Vijayawada. Addressing the Freshers’ Day celebrations at Dr. RVR NRI Institute of Technology (Deemed to be University), he emphasised that bold aspirations lead to new ideas and innovative outcomes. He urged students to focus on holistic development rather than limiting their ambitions to obtaining academic degrees. The celebrations, organised to welcome newly admitted first-year students, witnessed the participation of over 2,000 students, who showcased their talents through colourful singing and dancing performances. Prof. M.L.N. Rao, Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor of Rajiv Gandhi University of Knowledge Technologies (RGUKT-AP), said emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Quantum Technologies would drive major transformations over the next five to 10 years. He encouraged students to prepare themselves to contribute to the visions of Swarna Andhra Pradesh 2047 and Viksit Bharat 2047. NRI University Chairman and Chancellor Dr. Ravi Venkata Rao said the institution’s four-year academic programme aimed at shaping students into responsible, capable individuals equipped to overcome challenges and contribute meaningfully to society. Vice-Chancellor Dr. K.R.S. Sambasiva Rao urged students to make effective use of the university’s teaching and learning facilities and continuously upgrade their skills to become industry-ready professionals. Organising convener and Dean D. Suneetha, CEO, Pro-Vice-Chancellors, Registrar, Deans, Heads of Departments, faculty members and other dignitaries attended the celebrations. Published - November 07, 2026 11:17 pm IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentence

f086a0b616aada4a.title: D2C brands see 27% more orders ahead of Diwali; sales value up 45%: Report
f086a0b616aada4a.summary: Direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands in India shipped 27 per cent more orders a day in the run-up to Diwali this year than in the same period last year, while the value of goods sold jumped about 45 per cent, according to a report. ClickPost, an AI logistics automation and post-purchase platform for D2C and retail, analysed more than 8 crore orders placed on the websites of nearly 400 D2C brands. It compared the festive shopping windows of September 20 to November 5 this year and September 1 to October 17 last year. e85d14ba92076f05.title: Nallur toll plaza on Kolkata National Highway to be moved to Durainallur
e85d14ba92076f05.summary: Updated - November 08, 2026 01:39 am IST - CHENNAI The National Highways Authority of India has planned to shift the toll plaza at Nallur on the Chennai - Kolkata National Highway. It will be moved to Durainallur, which is about 13 km from the present location. The plaza is notorious for long waits during rush hours. Motorists fed up with waiting at the Nallur Plaza will get some relief from this move. “Residents of areas such as Karanodai, Janapanchathiram, Nallur and Periyapalayam will find it very convenient when the plaza is removed. There are several colleges in the area and the buses transporting students too wait in queue to cross the plaza on many occasions. Shifting of the plaza has been a long-time demand,” said K. Suresh Kumar, a resident. Ramesh, another resident, suggested that the width of the road be narrowed at that location. “It is now wider than the road width, making it difficult to cross. It would be helpful if the road stretch is normalised and shops regularised,” he said. Sources in the NHAI said that the existing location was no longer viable as a number of new roads have been laid in the surroundings making it possible for road users to avoid the plaza. This will lead to loss of revenue. “The plaza is also located inside municipal limits, making it pertinent to shift it outside. The contract of the current agency managing the plaza will get over by May next year. We hope to get the design ready for the new plaza by then,” explained a source. Around 50,000 passenger car units use that road on a daily basis. The plaza is also likely to be a multi-lane free flow tolling system without toll booths and operators. bf7eb2a5cf5df45f.title: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings files draft papers with Sebi for IPO
bf7eb2a5cf5df45f.summary: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings Ltd (HCCH), backed by The Coca-Cola Company and Jubilant Beverages, has filed its draft papers with the market regulator Sebi to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO). The proposed IPO will be entirely an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 99,74,61,456 equity shares by promoter Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte Ltd, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated November 6. Since the issue is entirely an OFS, the company will not receive any proceeds from the IPO, with the entire proceeds going to the selling shareholder.

fc952079d179daed.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:56 am IST - NEW DELHI Mohammed Shami in action. File | Photo Credit: Nirmal Harindran The BCCI on Saturday paid a glowing tribute Mohammad Shami, saying the wily India pacer defined an era of pace bowling in Test cricket. Shami announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday night. He ended his Test journey with 229 wickets from 64 matches, making him the sixth most successful pacer in Tests for the country behind Kapil Dev (434), Zaheer Khan, Ishant Sharma (both 311), Javagal Srinath (236), Jasprit Bumrah (234). "Thank you for defining an era of Indian pace bowling, Test Cap #279," wrote the BCCI on social media. Former India cricketers also joined in to congratulate Shami on a successful red ball career. If Shami did not get the wickets, he would still keep the pressure on the opposition. "Sad to see him go. I definitely though he had another 30-40 wickets left in him. Students of the film institute on Saturday (November 7, 2026) said that “This Diwali we choose to resist”, while authorities said they were “keen" to resume classes. “Diwali has always been a special occasion at SRFTI... But this year, the familiar celebrations are overshadowed by fear, uncertainty and an ongoing struggle for justice,” an official post by the SRFTI student union said on Saturday (November 7, 2026), a day before Deepavali. They also said that the day they are served justice will be Deepavali for them. “While the faculty and administration are ready to resume classes, a section of students continues to remain disengaged from academics and disrupt the functioning of the Institute through repeated violations of its rules and orders,” Registrar Deepak Kumar told The Hindu on Saturday (November 7, 2026). He further added that they are asking students to come forward for constructive dialogue. As of November 7, at least 25 students have received show cause notices, with 11 of them receiving them last Thursday (November 5, 2026). Six students have faced rustication, and one FIR has been registered against student union Vice-President Shubham. Shubham is one of the six students who got the rustication notice for allegedly vandalising the Vice-Chancellor Santosh Ajmeera’s office and manhandling him. However, all of these allegations have been denied by the students. According to the students, two contractual faculty members, and five resource persons of SRFTI have also been terminated from their jobs for showing solidarity with the students. As the classes remained suspended, the hostels and mess were also closed for students. 73d8046d11b387ed.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 11:35 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Mathematics forms the backbone of modern artificial intelligence (AI), with advanced AI capabilities, predictive power and logical reasoning deeply rooted in mathematical equations, frameworks and data algorithms, said Reheena Nasrin of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Addressing the valedictory session of a three-day international conference on “Computation Science and Intelligent Engineering”, organised by the Department of Mathematics in Siddhartha Academy of Higher Education (Deemed-to-be-University), she emphasised that strong mathematical foundations would remain essential for the future advancement of digital intelligence. The final-day technical sessions featured lectures by eminent experts. G. Sobhalatha of Sri Krishnadevaraya University, Anantapur, spoke on ‘Lexicographic Product Graph’, while Bukke Kiran Naik, a scientist from the National Institute of Technology (NIT), Rourkela, delivered a lecture on ‘Intelligent Thermodynamics’, focusing on data-driven systems optimisation and energy-water nexus solutions. Conference convener Charan announced that more than 200 research papers had been presented by academicians and researchers from reputed universities across India, reflecting the conference’s contribution to academic research and knowledge exchange. Certificates of participation and excellence were distributed to the paper presenters by the dignitaries. The valedictory session was attended by Vice-Chancellor P. Venkateswara Rao, Pro-Vice-Chancellor A.V. Ratna Prasad, dean D. Venkata Rao and registrar M. Ravichand. Head of the Mathematics Department Ch. Baby Rani, senior faculty members K. Hemalatha, J. Siva Ram Prasad and M.V.D.N.S. Madhavi, other faculty members, department heads, research scholars and students also participated in the programme. 39661e7999ffb000.title: Three investors offload 1.84% stake in Groww for ₹2,457 crore in bulk deals
39661e7999ffb000.summary: Peak XV Partners, Y Combinator and Goldman Sachs have sold a combined 2 per cent stake in Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of Groww, for Rs 2,457 crore, according to bulk deal data on the BSE and NSE. The three investors offloaded more than 11.52 crore shares, representing a combined 1.84 per cent stake in Groww on Friday, as per the data. US-based Peak XV Partners, through its arm Peak XV Partners Investments VI-1, sold more than 6 crore shares, and Goldman Sachs divested 4,380 shares of Groww on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). In addition, Y Combinator, through its arm YC Holdings II, LLC, disposed of 5.50 crore shares on the BSE. The shares were disposed of in the price range of Rs 211.09-215.20 apiece, taking the combined deal value to Rs 2,456.87 crore. Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs purchased 3.55 crore shares worth over Rs 764 crore. Details of other buyers of Groww's shares could not be identified on the exchanges. d607e15879d0bb8d.title: Bengaluru Metro conducts trial run of Blue Line train at Byappanahalli depot
d607e15879d0bb8d.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 11:42 pm IST - Bengaluru Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) conducted a trial run of a train on the test track at the Byappanahalli depot on Saturday as part of preparations for the much-awaited Blue Line. The trial involved checking electrical systems, assessing the readiness of rolling stock and identifying possible infringements along the track. BMRCL is expected to move testing to the main line shortly. An official said that the testing would resume next week, subject to the availability of workers following Deepavali. Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML) has manufactured the driverless trainset for the Blue Line. The Blue Line, comprising Metro Phases 2A and 2B, is a major infrastructure project connecting the city with Kempegowda International Airport. The K.R. Puram–airport stretch is 38.44-km long, while the K.R. Puram–Central Silk Board section covers 19.75 km. 7a6a76cada888f6f.title: DMK flays govt.’s decision to remit money in lieu of distributing rice to ration cardholders in U.T.
7a6a76cada888f6f.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 03:04 am IST - PUDUCHERRY Convenor of DMK’s Puducherry unit R. Siva has flayed the AINRC-BJP government for adopting the cash transfer mode instead of distributing free rice under the scheme in the Union Territory. In a statement, the DMK leader said the government had not distributed free rice through ration shops for the last nine months. Now, the government has remitted money into the accounts of ration cardholders in lieu of free rice meant for six months. The amount remitted by the government was based on a calculation of ₹43 per kg for the rice, he said. However, the cash remitted was not sufficient for buying rice due to cost escalation. The price of rice has gone up substantially in the open market and the money given by the government would be inadequate for the residents to buy the required quantity, he said. “The government’s decision to adopt Direct Benefit Transfer mode was a betrayal of the mandate given by the people. The Chief Minister had promised the voters to provide rice through ration shops. If the implementation of the scheme to distribute rice through ration shops would take more time, the government should remit more money considering the market rate of rice,” Mr. Siva said. 78b4dd6ccab6540f.title: Renovated bus terminus in Ranipet town opened for public use
78b4dd6ccab6540f.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:57 am IST - RANIPET Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspect the restored bus terminus in the town in the presence of transport and municipal officials. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement After more than four years of renovation work, the restored ₹13.55-crore integrated bus terminus on the Ranipet-Walajah Main Road was opened for public use, ahead of Deepavali. Officials of Ranipet municipality, which executed the multi-crore work, said that the old terminus was built more than five decades ago with very few facilities for commuters. “The restored terminus helps people board long-distance buses. The facility has better seating arrangements and safety features for commuters,” said S. Kumar, a commuter. Funded under Kalaignar Nagarpura Membattu Thittam 2022-23 that aims to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in the urban local bodies, work to restore the terminus was started in 2022. “The restored bus terminus will help commuters, especially women and senior citizens to board buses safely as round-the-clock surveillance is in place. A help desk is also available to guide commuters,” said D. Senthil Kumar, Commissioner, Ranipet municipality. Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspected the restored bus terminus in the town in the presence of transport and municipal officials. The restored bus terminus will operate buses to Bengaluru, Vellore, Vandavasi, Cheyyar, Chengam, Arcot, Ranipet, Coimbatore, Salem, Kancheepuram, Hosur, and Dharmapuri. Among civic amenities, the terminus has a purified drinking water facility, solar-powered LED streetlights, digital timing boards, feeding room, a police booth, and CCTV cameras. A police outpost will also be set up in the coming days. Every day, on an average, more than 200 buses operated by Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation ply from the terminus. Commuters said that additional buses to towns such as Tiruvannamalai, Sholinghur, Arcot, Gingee, and Kancheepuram should be operated at the terminus. Publ

2052a510689062eb.title: Greek-themed Salaam Souk to be held at Palace Grounds in Bengaluru on November 8
2052a510689062eb.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:56 am IST - Bengaluru The Karnataka Tourism Department is supporting, ‘Salaam Souk – The Big Fat Greek Souk’, an event showcasing the colours, cuisine, music and Mediterranean culture of Greece to people in Bengaluru. Scheduled to be held on November 8 in Palace Grounds, the event marks the eighth edition of Salaam Souk and its first Greek-themed edition. It is an initiative of The Tribe & Co that has previously presented cultural themes inspired by Morocco, Turkey, Uzbekistan, India and Dubai. The festival has been designed to recreate the feel of a Greek street market, combining Mediterranean-inspired food, fashion, art, music, home décor, beauty and wellness experiences. The event will feature 35 food stalls, 150 retail stalls, live bands, fire shows and aerial performances, offering visitors a distinctive Greek-inspired cultural experience in Bengaluru. 8464144f1a0e52ff.title: 108 ambulance network geared up to handle emergencies
8464144f1a0e52ff.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:55 am IST - CHENNAI In view of Deepavali, the 108 ambulance network is prepared to handle all types of emergencies. All ambulances across the State have been strategically positioned at identified hotspots to ensure that emergency care reaches the needy at the earliest. According to a press release, this proactive deployment will help in minimising the response time and thereby increasing the life-saved percentage. The network, especially in metro cities, has clocked an average response time of less than seven minutes, and is focused on sustaining and further improving the same. The “EMRI GHS 108 Ambulance Services”, based on the previous year experiences, have taken precautionary measures with regard to deployment of ambulances in identified Deepavali hotspot areas, where more number of fire/ burns and assault cases are expected in the respective locations. Last year, the network received 26,000 calls requiring emergency services across Tamil Nadu during Deepavali. The Emergency Response Centre for helplines 108, 104 and 102 are working with full strength under three shifts. All support staff are working in coordination with respective district authorities, the release said. A medical protocol is being developed to transfer the patient based on their criticality from a lower facility to a higher facility, while inter-hospital transfer of critical patients is earmarked through Advanced Life Support ambulances based on separate despatch criteria. A dedicated Inter Facility Transfer help desk is also functioning, the release said. Through these cells, the university will conduct placement drives, besides holding offline and online skill training essential for employment. 59f706d6e2da936e.title: Rahul questions E20 petrol ethanol levels, cites Karnataka test results
59f706d6e2da936e.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday attacked the Modi government over the rollout of E20 petrol, citing test results of samples collected by the Karnataka government, and asked the Centre to come clean on the actual ethanol content in fuel being sold across the country. In a post in Hindi on X, Gandhi said, "E20 turned into 420 stealing petrol from the public's cars!" The reference was to Section 420 of the erstwhile Indian Penal Code, which dealt with cheating. Gandhi said the government claims that petrol contains 20 per cent ethanol but tests conducted on samples collected from seven districts in Karnataka had revealed higher levels. "The Karnataka government collected petrol samples from 7 districts and had them tested at an accredited lab. Look at the results 11 out of 14 samples contained more than 20 per cent ethanol; 31.2 per cent at IOCL, 30.5 per cent at HPCL; IOCL, HPCL, BPCL, Nayara, Shell whether government-owned or private all exceeded the limit," he claimed.

74f5ce093329eb6c.title: Two youths arrested for possessing narcotics in Vellore
74f5ce093329eb6c.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:54 am IST - VELLORE Two youths were arrested by Vellore South police for possession of 1300 narcotic tablets (Tapentadol) near the fort complex in Vellore town on Saturday. The police identified them as R. Vinoth, 23, and his friend B. Manimaran, 23. They were residents of Vellore town. Initial inquiry revealed that based on a tip-off to Vellore SP N.U. Sivaraman, special teams were formed to conduct surprise checks in public places in the district. During a surprise check near the fort complex, the team apprehended the suspects. They checked the duo and their bags, where they found a huge quantity of pharmaceutical drugs in them. Investigation found that the gang had placed an order for tablets with pharmacies online. The tablets were sent by couriers to them. The police said the duo were on their way to the railway station to go to Chennai, where they planned to sell the drugs. A case was registered and arrested persons were lodged in Central Prison in Vellore. A probe is under way. 37bb49dfea8ff924.title: Gang held near Vaniyambadi for burglary
37bb49dfea8ff924.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:54 am IST - TIRUPATTUR A gang of five persons were arrested by Vaniyambadi Taluk police in Tirupattur on Saturday for stealing 52 sovereigns of gold jewellery, one kilogram of silver objects and around ₹20,000 lakh cash from the house of a painter recently. The arrested persons were identified as K. Naveen, 26, T. Parthiban, 30, S. Gopinath, 39, G. Manikandan, 40, and C. Sarathkumar, 25. They are previous offenders and have theft cases against them in Salem, Dharmapuri, Tirupattur, Thanjavur, and Pudukottai. Initial inquiry revealed that the victim, R. Prabhakaran, 39, was living with his family including wife Geetha (34) and mother Ambika (65) in the house near Vaniyambadi town a few days ago when the gang barged into the house. The police said the gang allegedly tied R. Prabhakaran, 39, and his family and stole the valuables from the house before fleeing the spot. Mr. Prabhakaran managed to untie himself and alerted Vaniyambadi Taluk police. Special teams were formed to nab the suspects. The police also analysed CCTV camera footage to identify suspects. The suspects were traced to a hideout in Thanjavur and were arrested. A car used by the gang was also seized. The police said that members of the gang befriended each other when they were serving jail sentences. They travel to various parts of the State and stay in a locality before indulging in burglary. ef79ad7ceb40913e.title: Techie arrested for attempting to snatch woman’s chain using pepper spray
ef79ad7ceb40913e.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:46 am IST - CHENNAI A 46-year-old project manager at an IT company was arrested for allegedly attacking a woman with pepper spray in an attempt to snatch her gold chain on a pedestrian footbridge near Tambaram Sanatorium. Police said he turned to chain snatching to repay debts accumulated through losses in online trading. The victim, Bhuvaneswari, 24, an MBA graduate from Chitlapakkam, works with a private financial firm in Tambaram. 27b94618dc63453b.title: Divi's Labs Q2 result: Net profit rises 64% to ₹1,127 cr on higher revenue
27b94618dc63453b.summary: Divi's Laboratories Ltd on Saturday posted a sharp 63.57 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 1,127 crore in the September quarter due to higher revenues. The company posted a net profit of Rs 689 crore in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year, a regulatory filing said. Revenue from operations rose 35.39 per cent to Rs 3,676 crore during the second quarter of FY27 from Rs 2,715 crore a year earlier, it said. Its total expenses rose to Rs 2,265 crore in the period under review from Rs 1,948 crore a year ago, it added. The company's net profit for the first half of the current fiscal year, however, declined 35.39 per cent to Rs 2,029 crore from Rs 2,568 crore in the year-ago period, the filing added.

34907735bc26c903.title: RPF steps up Deepavali vigil, apprehends five with firecrackers at Chennai Central, Egmore
34907735bc26c903.summary: Updated - November 08, 2026 01:50 am IST - CHENNAI With a view to ensuring passenger safety during the Deepavali festival, the Railway Protection Force (RPF), Chennai Division, Southern Railway, has intensified surveillance and preventive checks at major railway stations to curb illegal transportation of firecrackers and other inflammable materials. During special checks conducted on Friday, RPF personnel apprehended five persons carrying firecrackers at Chennai Central and Chennai Egmore railway stations in two separate operations. At Chennai Central, four persons were intercepted while attempting to board passenger trains with firecrackers. Three were stopped before boarding the Chennai Central–Jolarpettai Yelagiri Express, while another was intercepted before boarding the Chennai Central–Thiruvananthapuram Express. Four separate cases were registered against them under Section 164 of the Railways Act, 1989. At Chennai Egmore, RPF personnel apprehended a 25-year-old man carrying a box of firecrackers and registered a case under the same provision. Meanwhile, as part of its efforts to sensitise passengers ahead of Deepavali, the RPF conducted a Jan Jagaran awareness programme at Chennai Beach Railway Station on Friday. Passengers were cautioned against carrying firecrackers and other explosive materials on trains, as they could cause fires and explosions, endangering lives and railway property. They were informed about the provisions of Section 164 of the Railways Act, which prescribes imprisonment for up to three years for unauthorised possession or transportation of explosives on railway premises or trains. During the awareness drive, nine persons were apprehended for unauthorised trespassing and fined ₹500 each under Section 147 of the Railways Act, taking the total collection to ₹4,500. 62e36a797e1e03cf.title: Delivery firm employee arrested for stealing mobile phones
62e36a797e1e03cf.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:57 am IST - CHENNAI The Guindy police have arrested a 21-year-old employee of a private online delivery company for allegedly stealing two mobile phones from the firm’s returned goods inventory. Police said the complainant, Bhagavathi Murugan, 40, a resident of Guindy, works as a manager in the security and loss prevention department of a private online delivery company in the Guindy Industrial Estate. According to the complaint, Prathumna Krishna, an employee of the company, was responsible for inspecting goods returned by customers when deliveries could not be completed and processing them for return as per the prescribed procedures. When Bhagavathi Murugan recently checked the returned consignments, he found that two mobile phones received back on October 21 and 28, were missing. An internal check revealed that Krishna had allegedly stolen the phones. The police registered a case and examined CCTV footage and conducted inquiries at the company before arresting Prathumna Krishna, 21, a resident of Subramania Swamy Koil West Street, West Saidapet. Police recovered one mobile phone from him and ₹10,000, which he had allegedly obtained by selling the other stolen phone. 9256e15f091d794d.title: Centre allows transfer of prisoners between Chandigarh, other states
9256e15f091d794d.summary: The Centre has extended the Punjab Police and Correctional Services Act, 2006, to the Union Territory of Chandigarh, introducing provisions for the transfer of prisoners between states and Union territories and changes to the functioning of the prison administration. The notification, issued under Section 87 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, extends the Punjab legislation to the Union Territory of Chandigarh with certain modifications, according to a notification issued by the Union Home Ministry on Friday. The amended provisions deal with the transfer of prisoners between Chandigarh and other states or Union territories. Under the provisions, prisoners serving sentences in Chandigarh, including life imprisonment, may be transferred to prisons in another state or Union territory with the consent of the government concerned and an order issued by the Chandigarh administrator. The amendments also provide for the transfer of undertrial prisoners in the interest of Chandigarh's .

09b406db0ac57bf2.title: Five killed, over a dozen injured as gunman opens fire in Poland's Krakow
09b406db0ac57bf2.summary: Five people were killed and more than a dozen injured after a gunman opened fire Saturday afternoon in a market square in Krakow, Poland, police said. The gunman aimed at random people as he drove by the city's Main Square, Krakow police said. Police officers are among the wounded. The perpetrator was shot and wounded during a confrontation with police. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, in a post on X, said police are investigating the attack. Other details were not immediately available. Krakow is the second-largest city in Poland and roughly 250 kilometres from the capital, Warsaw.

Industrialist Gautam Adani and NCP leader Praful Patel had also visited the hospital. Pawar was initially admitted to Pune's Ruby Hall Clinic on November 2 and discharged on November 4. The same day, he was admitted to the Mumbai hospital.

8f2075cd50333015.title: UP govt hikes DA by 5%, employees to get arrears retrospectively from Jul 1
8f2075cd50333015.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has hiked the Dearness Allowance (DA) by 5 per cent for state government employees, staff in aided educational and technical institutions, regular and full-time employees of urban local bodies, work-charged employees, and those serving on UGC pay scales. Employees will now receive a Dearness Allowance of 63 per cent, up from 58 per cent. The increased rate will be effective from July 1, 2026, the state government said in a statement on Saturday. A government order was also issued in this regard on Saturday. The enhanced dearness allowance will be paid along with the regular salary for November 2026. This government decision will benefit lakhs of employees across the state. The move by the Yogi Adityanath government will provide relief not only to the state's regular employees but also to staff in aided educational institutions, urban local bodies, and other eligible categories of employees, the statement said.

0bd4985135c1371a.title: India-US trade deal: What midterm elections mean for trade policy, tariff and export sectors? Experts explain
0bd4985135c1371a.summary: As India and the US work to finalise a long-awaited trade deal, the ruling Republicans' major electoral loss in the recently concluded US midterm polls has raised crucial questions: How may this flip in the US Congress affect the India-US negotiations? Will the setback to US President Donald Trump's party give India room to negotiate? Experts believe that the Republican Party's stinging loss in the midterm elections, which shifted the balance of power in the US Congress , may push Trump to accelerate negotiations that had been reportedly stalled over tariff concerns. This, however, may not make the "US trade policy less restrictive", they said. Another expert explained why India may get some room to negotiate on “substance rather than under deadline pressure”. Professor Rituparna Kaushik, Assistant Professor at FLAME University, told Mint that the midterm election results will not rewrite US trade policy overnight. This is because "the Section 301 and Section 232 duties [under which tariffs were imposed] rest on executive authority and any rollback faces a presidential veto," he said. He believed that a Democratic Congress with oversight powers "makes abrupt tariff escalation politically harder, which gives India room to negotiate on substance rather than under deadline pressure". "Labour-intensive exporters in textiles, apparel, and gems and jewellery stand to gain most from that stability," he noted. On India’s strategy, Kaushik said New Delhi must "secure a predictable, rules-based tariff schedule rather than chase short-term concessions, and to broaden engagement beyond the White House to Congress and US states." "At the same time, India must keep diversifying through the EU agreement and other partners, so the US remains a key market but not a single point of vulnerability. On agriculture and dairy, India should hold firm, as US farm-lobby pressure cuts across party lines," he added. Ajay Srivastava, Founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), said

bbc6be00bd36b3cc.title: Investing in US stocks from India: Check how these 5 platforms stack up
bbc6be00bd36b3cc.summary: More Indian investors are buying US and other overseas stocks through apps and brokers. Indian investors who want US and other overseas stocks have more routes than ever. Mutual funds have hit the industry-wide $7 billion SEBI cap on overseas investments, so more investors are going direct under the RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), which allows up to $250,000 per person a financial year. Demand is moving the market quickly. Platforms are adding features, changing how they are set up and launching products at pace, so it helps to know what each one does best and whether it fits your needs. This story looks at five: INDmoney, Interactive Brokers (IBKR), Vested Finance, Paasa and ZFunds. Business Standard heard from executives at four of the five and spoke to two investors who have used most of them. Four things separate these platforms. Notes: Vested charges $5 per USD withdrawal, which mainly applies to NRI accounts. “Size” figures are as reported by each company and are not like-for-like. Launched in 2019, INDmoney targets salaried retail investors and runs as an IFSCA-licensed Global Access Provider in GIFT City. It also files income tax returns for users, with Schedule FA filled in. The company reports $3.5 billion in global investing assets and plans to add European and Southeast Asian exchanges by December 2026. “We are not building a platform exclusively for wealthy individuals making large international remittances,” founder and CEO Ashish Kashyap told Business Standard . Founded in 1978, IBKR is a direct broker with no Indian intermediary and reported about 5.7 million client accounts in October 2026. It offers UCITS ETFs and several overseas markets, but has a complex interface, manual tax work and bank wire fees of ₹500–1,000 plus GST per transfer. Pranay Kapoor, a tech professional and YouTuber who has tried most of these apps, told Business Standard that with IBKR “there is no middleman.” Kapoor sends money in large tranches so the flat wire fee

6bb06909f49a0814.title: Book launched to honour work of child rights activist Thomas Jayaraj
6bb06909f49a0814.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:32 am IST - Chennai: The Centre for Child Rights and Development (CCRD) launched a book titled Voices of Transformation – Walking the path of Thomas Jayaraj towards a Culture of Child Rights to honour the contributions of Thomas Jayaraj, who passed away in 2021. He was at the forefront of many child rights initiatives at both the State and national levels. The book was released at the Madras School of Social Work (MSSW) on Friday by Sudha Ramalingam, senior advocate of Madras High Court. D. Geetha, Managing Trustee, CCRD, received the first copy. Stegana Jency L.T., Director of CCRD, said the team was committed to carrying forward the principles of Mr. Jayaraj. “We are launching this book because everything Mr. Jayaraj did should t become a guide for future leaders,” she said. Mr. Jayaraj’s daughter, Liby Rajam, said her father not only spoke for child rights, but also built a community that would continue to advocate for child rights in the future. Meanwhile, Ms. Ramalingam said there was considerable work to be done in this field. “When it comes to child rights and development, we must get the youngsters involved,” she said. Journalist and activist Aishwarya, and Antony Stephen, assistant professor and head of partnerships, MSSW, spoke about child rights advocacy. b37d55aed236271b.title: India's foreign exchange reserves drop by $2.69 billion to $717 billion
b37d55aed236271b.summary: India's forex reserves dropped by USD 2.691 billion to USD 717.056 billion during the week ended October 30, the RBI said on Friday. In the previous week, the forex kitty had reduced by USD 1.269 billion to USD 719.748 billion. The reserves had touched an all-time high of USD 785.706 billion during the week ended September 4, driven by a heavy flow of currency as part of a special concessional swap for deposits from the diaspora through which banks raised a record USD 133 billion, but have been on a decline ever since. Experts attribute this decline to the deployment of the FCNR(B) resources and also to currency defence put up by RBI through dollar sales. During the week ended October 30, foreign currency assets, a major component of reserves, decreased by USD 2.088 billion to USD 591.118 billion, according to the data released by Reserve Bank of India (RBI). d47a5aca9eff8a29.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 03:20 am IST - New Delhi Every unit holding stocks will have to update details on the Food Stock Portal every Friday, the Food Ministry said in a statement. | Photo Credit: M. Srinath With rice prices rising due to a deficient and uneven monsoon, the Centre on Friday (November 7, 2026) directed traders, retailers, wholesalers, processors and millers across the country to declare their rice and paddy stocks and allowed five southern States to impose stock limits to prevent hoarding. Under a November 6 order, all traders and wholesalers, retailers, large retail chains and processors and millers in all States and Union Territories must declare stocks under six categories — Basmati rice, non-Basmati premium rice, non-Basmati rice, parboiled rice, broken rice and paddy. Every unit holding stocks will have to update details on the Food Stock Portal (foodstock.dfpd.gov.in) every Friday, the Food Ministry said in a statement. Units that are not registered on the portal or that violate stock limits will face action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. In a separate letter, also dated November 6, the Centre has given its consent to Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana to impose stock limits on paddy and rice through control orders. The limits will remain in force till January 31, 2027. The Centre and States will monitor implementation to ensure adequate availability and prevent hoarding and black marketing, an official statement said. To improve availability, the Centre is allocating additional rice stocks to NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar for sale as Bharat Rice, and has asked them to explore all possible distribution channels, especially in the southern States. The Centre has also doubled the target for rice sales through e-auction under the Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) for 2026-27 from 25 lakh tonnes to 50 lakh tonnes. Around 25 lakh tonnes had been sold to private parties by October 31,

0aa42e8c21ff097a.title: T.N. govt. allocates monthly maintenance fund of ₹1,000 to 12,646 VAO offices
0aa42e8c21ff097a.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:50 am IST - CHENNAI The Tamil Nadu government has issued an order allocating ₹1,000 each as a monthly maintenance fund to 12,646 Village Administrative Officer (VAO) offices functioning across the State, involving an annual expenditure of ₹15.18 crore. A Government Order to this effect was issued by the Revenue and Disaster Management Department on Friday. It follows an announcement made by Minister for Revenue and Disaster Management K.A. Sengottaiyan in the Assembly on August 17 during the Budget session. The maintenance fund will be used to arrange drinking water facilities, seating, ramps for persons with disabilities and other amenities for members of the public visiting VAO offices to obtain birth certificates, death certificates, patta, chitta, certificates for small and marginal farmers, legal heir certificates, income certificates, nativity certificates, community certificates and first-generation graduate certificates, among others. The monthly maintenance fund will be credited to the VAOs’ salaries under the head of maintenance allowance. The government has also allocated ₹8.85 crore towards this fund for the period from September 2026 to March 2027 in the current financial year. e224bcf6fc2f1be1.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:52 am IST - CHENNAI The Tamil Nadu government has appointed three Special Public Prosecutors to conduct the trial in the cases booked against Gem Granites owner R. Veeramani under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012. In an order issued on Friday, the State Government said considering the sensitive and complex nature of the cases, K.R. Sankaran, M. Sandhiya and Swami Subramanian were appointed as Special Public Prosecutors under Section 31(1) of the Act to conduct prosecution of the case investigated by the Special Investigation Team (SIT). Mr Veeramani and his associates are facing seven cases under the POCSO Act and one case of abetment to suicide of a minor in 2004. 23850def92ab4fc4.title: Agasthyamalai conservation case: SC directs temporary and non-resident silk cotton cultivators not eligible for protection under FRA Act
23850def92ab4fc4.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 01:47 am IST - NEW DELHI The Supreme Court directed on Friday that individuals with temporary residence in the Agasthyamalai biosphere or those living entirely outside the forest boundaries cannot be classified as traditional forest dwellers merely for cultivating silk cotton within the forest. “Persons falling in Category II and Category III, as classified in the additional affidavit of September 6 filed by Department of Revenue, State of Tamil Nadu, shall be excluded from consideration as forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers for the purposes of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 or FRA Act,” a Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta directed. According to Tamil Nadu’s own affidavit, 232 persons are cultivating the forest area with temporary residence while 2,767 persons who occupy 2,867.70 hectares land are residing outside the forest boundary and are managing silk cotton cultivation. The order was passed in furtherance of a May 2026 judgment, which had issued various directions for a structured and time-bound process of eviction, rehabilitation and ecological restoration in the forest areas. The court had ordered the preparation of a division-wise eviction plan, removal of encroachments, and action against identified government servants. It had imposed a prohibition on approval or commencement of new non-forestry activities or diversion proposals within the Agasthyamalai landscape, and directed continued monitoring of the area by the Central Empowered Committee (CEC). Justice Mehta, who authored the order, held the State government “primarily responsible” for delaying the receipt of claims under the 2006 Act. 3254ea801e375485.title: Demonetisation and the health costs of cash shortages
3254ea801e375485.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:15 am IST Liquidity is an economic determinant of health’ | Photo Credit: THE HINDU/MANJUNATH H.S. On November 8, 2016, 86% of India’s currency by value — in the form of ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes — ceased to be legal tender at just four hours’ notice. The stated objectives included curbing counterfeit currency and black money and accelerating the adoption of digital payments. It was among the largest transitory liquidity shocks engineered in a cash-reliant economy. Nearly all demonetised currency returned – some 99.3% as per Reserve Bank of India data – and broader financial indicators such as interest rates and deposits remained stable. As Chodorow-Reich et al. in their influential 2020 Quarterly Journal of Economics study have documented, the direct effect was a temporary reduction in the stock of money in the economy. 8da91880dd5ffb6b.title: Minister inaugurates dialysis centre
8da91880dd5ffb6b.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:35 am IST - CHENNAI Health Minister K.G. Arunraj inaugurated the “Rotary Kamdar Dialysis Centre” at the Government Peripheral Hospital in Anna Nagar on Friday. The centre, which was established by Rotary District 3234 in association with the Rotary Club of Chennai Kilpauk through a collaborative public-private partnership, aims at strengthening public healthcare infrastructure and improving access to essential dialysis services for patients requiring regular renal care. The initiative has been supported by the Pushpavati Babulal Kamdar Charitable Trust, Rotary Clubs of Chennai, and Wockhardt Foundation, in collaboration with Government Peripheral Hospital, Anna Nagar. The Rotary Clubs and Kamdar Charitable Trust have jointly provided medical equipment worth approximately ₹1.6 crore, including 10 dialysis machines, a Reverse Osmosis plant, and an effluent treatment plant. The centre is designed to serve up to 30 patients per day. The day-to-day dialysis expenses will be funded through the Chief Minister’s Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme, a press release said. Speaking at the inauguration, Dr. Arunraj said, “Healthcare is a shared responsibility, and it is important for all of us to contribute towards the well-being of society. The role played by Rotary in the eradication of polio is a wonderful example of what collective efforts and partnerships can achieve. We must build on this spirit of collaboration and work together towards our mission of eradicating cervical cancer.” The District Rotaract Council, Rotary International District 3234, in association with the Rotary Club of Chennai Kilpauk, also organised a Blood Donation Drive. D. Suresh Jain, District Governor 2026–27, Rotary International District 3234 and J.B. Kamdar, Managing Trustee, Pushpavati Babulal Kamdar Charitable Trust, were present. ecdfcae84b13fb27.title: Unhappy Milind Deora shoots a letter to BMC chief over event exclusion
ecdfcae84b13fb27.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 04:22 am IST - MUMBAI Shiv Sena MP Milind Deora. | Photo Credit: Emmanual Yogini Member of Parliament Milind Deora wrote a letter to Ashwini Bhide, Commissioner of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), on Friday regarding an omission. Mr. Deora stated that the BMC did not invite him to an inauguration in Colaba. Mr. Deora is a Rajya Sabha MP from the Shiv Sena, which is part of the ruling alliance in Maharashtra. Colaba falls in the area he represents. The event was for a housing project under the Ashray Yojana on November 6, 2026, with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde attending. Speaker Rahul Narwekar, Mayor Ritu Tawde, and Deputy Mayor Sanjay Ghadi also attended. The BMC distributed keys to workers under the scheme. Mr. Deora wrote in the letter that representatives require notice of events in the areas they represent, noting that the event took place without informing him. He wrote that coordination and courtesy towards representatives must accompany initiatives, stating that representatives need to receive information about developments for the people they serve. The MP requested Mr. Bhide to look into the matter and asked the Commissioner to ensure that protocol is followed to prevent an omission. He requested that officials receive advice to ensure coordination with representatives for functions.
