04b27ca4a8352a99.title: Supreme Court decision on BBMB arrears a victory for Himachal, says CM Sukhu
04b27ca4a8352a99.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 01:30 am IST - New Delhi Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. | Photo Credit: ANI Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed the Supreme Court’s decision directing Punjab and Haryana to supply 11,973 million units of electricity to the State over 20 years towards its outstanding dues from the Bhakra-Nangal and Beas hydroelectric projects a historic victory for its people. The order settles a decades-old dispute over Himachal Pradesh’s 7.19% share in the power generated from the projects. The State will receive nearly 60 crore units annually during the lean season, generating an estimated revenue of ₹10,000 crore to ₹20,000 crore over the 20-year period, depending on electricity prices, Mr. Sukhu said in a statement. He said the decision could fetch the State additional revenue of up to ₹1,000 crore annually. Even at ₹6 per unit, Himachal Pradesh would earn at least ₹500 crore a year, while a rate of ₹13-14 per unit would significantly increase the returns. Mr. Sukhu attributed the outcome to the State government’s sustained legal battle and determination to secure its financial rights. He described it as the fourth major success in protecting Himachal Pradesh’s interests, citing earlier victories in matters relating to Wildflower Hall, the Kishau Dam among others. The Chief Minister said the government was also pursuing its claims over the Shanan Power Project and the water cess. The additional revenue, he said, would be used to strengthen education and healthcare, improve road infrastructure, generate employment and ensure timely payment of financial benefits to government employees. Congratulating the State’s nearly 75 lakh residents, Mr. Sukhu said protecting its resources and making Himachal Pradesh self-reliant remained a top priority for his government. 70659eda1e845ccd.summary: Gland Pharma on Friday posted a 58.29 per cent rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 290.75 crore in the September quarter, driven by strong execution across businesses. The company had reported a net profit of Rs 183.68 crore in the year-ago period. The pharmaceutical company's revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,833.58 crore in the quarter under review from Rs 1,486.87 crore a year ago, the company said in a regulatory filing. Total expenses also rose to Rs 1,471.69 crore in the July-September period from Rs 1,287.12 crore a year earlier, it said. The company launched four molecules -- Sugammadex, Erythromycin, Fluorouracil and Atropine sulfate -- in the US this quarter, it said in a release. cee9fdc5046b6afa.title: Rural women narrate stories on how Gruha Lakshmi scheme helped build their lives
cee9fdc5046b6afa.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:07 am IST - Bengaluru Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar admiring a handmade beaded toy cradle gifted by one of the beneficiaries of the Gruha Lakshmi scheme at his home office in Bengaluru on Friday. | Photo Credit: ANI Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar’s interaction with Gruha Lakshmi scheme beneficiaries in Bengaluru on Friday turned out to be a forum for hearing stories about how the monthly cash deposit by the scheme helped poor women not just build their lives, but also make significant achievements like helping their wards pursue higher education. At the interaction, which was held at the Chief Minister’s home office to get feedback from beneficiaries on the occasion of the scheme completing three years of implementation, a woman from Chikkamagaluru district said: “My son is studying MBBS in Koppal. I paid the fee of around ₹59,000 using the Gruha Lakshmi money. Thanks to the Shakti (free bus travel for women) scheme, it has been convenient for me to visit my son frequently.” Another woman from Channarayapatna said she was able to send her daughter to Malaysia for a dance performance with the help of Gruha Lakshmi money along with the family’s savings. An aged woman from Laxmeshwar taluk in Gadag district emotionally observed, “The Gruha Lakshmi money has helped senior women buy their medicines and lead a life of dignity.” A woman from Kudligi taluk explained how their self-help group pooled the scheme money to take up sheep rearing. Everyone was surprised when she said that the group that started with five sheep now had 300 sheep and employed five men to look after them. All the beneficiaries made a fervent appeal to the Chief Minister not to stop the scheme. Responding positively to the scheme, the Chief Minister declared that there was no question of discontinuing the scheme.
